eukruDKTdw.main_concern: The dual-reference advantage in Eq. 3 pools group statistics and does not keep a prefix-matched cue versus no-cue comparison, so the claimed state-local credit assignment is not supported and gains may come from a cue bonus.

c7glL6ugGz.one_liner: Interactive multi-character world model with an evolving 3D voxel map and entity records that renders per-player video from persistent state.
c7glL6ugGz.problem: Video-based world models can look correct while the underlying state is unchanged, so removed blocks reappear, health stays static and off-screen NPCs leave no lasting traces when characters share a scene.
c7glL6ugGz.method: MI-World couples multi-character simulation with an evolving 3D voxel map and structured entity records. Scene completion fills unobserved terrain without overwriting established coordinates, player and NPC controls update voxel occupancy and attributes through a shared transition model, and perspective video is rendered from the updated canonical state.
c7glL6ugGz.key_idea: Keep a canonical 3D voxel state with entity records that scene completion cannot overwrite, update it through a shared transition model, and render each viewpoint from it.
c7glL6ugGz.evidence: A new dataset of 45,572 synchronized multi-character trajectories with annotated interaction events; cross-view consistency FVD against gamma-World and Solaris, and recovery of reference block edits and attacks under recorded controls.
c7glL6ugGz.claimed_gains: Cross-view consistency FVD of 240.7, compared with 280.0 for gamma-World and 443.1 for Solaris.
c7glL6ugGz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating unknown-region completion from deliberate state edits is a clear mechanism for persistent multi-character interaction, and that the dataset is useful, with improvements over the evaluated baselines.
c7glL6ugGz.main_concern: Experiments omit a comparison with PERSIST and component ablations, and leave closed-loop NPC behavior, shared-world consistency across characters and long rollouts without quantitative evaluation.

qoMHdpE2ka.one_liner: Nonparametric prototype inference for long-tailed deep clustering combining denoising-based support, repulsive Dirichlet-process prior and prototype exchange.
qoMHdpE2ka.problem: In long-tailed deep clustering, dense head regions take redundant prototype capacity, causing head-class over-segmentation and tail-class absorption.
qoMHdpE2ka.method: Builds a semantic support measure from denoising consistency as the base of a Dirichlet-process reference law, derives a Gibbs-tilted prototype prior with a log-determinantal redundancy constraint, reallocates redundant prototype slots to under-covered stable regions by cardinality-preserving exchange, and injects the result through an identity-initialized residual adapter in a finite alternating MAP pipeline that needs no labels, class frequencies or class number.
qoMHdpE2ka.key_idea: A log-determinantal repulsive prior over denoising-supported prototypes suppresses redundant head prototypes, and cardinality-preserving exchange moves their slots to uncovered tail regions.
qoMHdpE2ka.evidence: Long-tailed and balanced clustering benchmarks against competitive baselines, with analyses of estimated cluster cardinality (abstract truncated).
qoMHdpE2ka.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework coherently addresses prototype-allocation bias with complementary components and shows consistent gains on long-tailed and balanced benchmarks.
qoMHdpE2ka.main_concern: Hyperparameter and candidate-inventory choices that drive the estimated cluster count are not systematically evaluated, direct head-versus-tail allocation analysis is missing, and some baseline numbers differ from the paper they appear copied from.

53DcN4OkMM.one_liner: Benchmark and dataset of human play across 100+ task-platform settings for training and evaluating robot world models beyond visual quality.
53DcN4OkMM.problem: Action-conditioned world models must capture physical interactions beyond individual task execution patterns, but existing play datasets are limited in task, robot platform and observation diversity.
53DcN4OkMM.method: Integrates human-play data collection with world-model training and evaluation over ten manipulation and interaction categories and over 100 task-platform settings in real and simulated environments, adding action-consistency and task-progress-consistency metrics, closed-loop policy evaluation and in-model reinforcement learning.
53DcN4OkMM.key_idea: Broad human play across embodiments, with evaluation by action and task-progress consistency, tests whether world models reflect supplied actions and support policy optimization.
53DcN4OkMM.evidence: World models (Cosmos Nano and Edge and GigaWorld per reviewers) evaluated on visual, action-consistency and task-progress metrics, plus small-scale policy evaluation and RL experiments.
53DcN4OkMM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dataset is much broader than prior play datasets across robots, collection schemes and cameras, and that evaluating beyond visual fidelity exposes model-ranking differences.
53DcN4OkMM.main_concern: The new evaluators (inverse-dynamics and progress scores) lack independent validation, the play-data comparison is not matched for training exposure, and the policy-evaluation and RL experiments are small.

t20iiH2RlD.one_liner: Feed-forward online reconstruction of human, object and scene from monocular video with recurrent object and contact states.
t20iiH2RlD.problem: Existing feed-forward methods handle either human-object or human-scene reconstruction, methods that recover all three rely on per-sequence optimization, and the manipulated object is the least visible part of the interaction.
t20iiH2RlD.method: Extends a recurrent human-scene state with object and human-object contact representations that produce an interaction-conditioned pose hypothesis and feed interaction back to the human, then corrects the hypothesis with visual evidence gathered at canonical points of the known object template.
t20iiH2RlD.key_idea: An interaction-conditioned object pose hypothesis from the human state is corrected by visual evidence at canonical template points, and object-to-human feedback also refines the human.
t20iiH2RlD.evidence: BEHAVE for human-object reconstruction and EMDB for world-grounded human reconstruction, compared with feed-forward baselines such as UniCon3R and Human3R.
t20iiH2RlD.claimed_gains: Reduces combined human-object reconstruction error by 24% over the strongest feed-forward baseline on BEHAVE (the abstract is truncated before its human-improvement claim).
t20iiH2RlD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly reconstructing human, object and scene in one feed-forward pass is a worthwhile extension and that human reconstruction improves over direct baselines such as UniCon3R and Human3R.
t20iiH2RlD.main_concern: The claim that joint object reasoning improves the human is not ablated (EMDB-2 has few manipulated objects and the training data differs from UniCon3R), and the method needs a known 3D object template.

m72TXFkMUn.one_liner: Builds a CAD program from a mesh one operation at a time, comparing target and current geometry after each step.
m72TXFkMUn.problem: Most AI CAD reverse-engineering systems emit the whole program in a single pass without inspecting intermediate geometry, unlike engineers who check what remains to be modeled after each feature.
m72TXFkMUn.method: CADENA grows a sequence of CAD operations one at a time, comparing the target mesh with the geometry predicted so far at every step, using a CadQuery-based operation vocabulary and stepwise SFT plus RL training per reviewers, and the paper adds CADENA-Bench for mechanical parts.
m72TXFkMUn.key_idea: Each next CAD operation is predicted from a geometry-only comparison between the target and the executed partial program, instead of generating the whole program at once.
m72TXFkMUn.evidence: CADENA-Bench plus DeepCAD, Fusion 360, MCB and BenchCAD, with a same-backbone single-pass comparison and ablations.
m72TXFkMUn.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract, which says CADENA outperforms prior methods on all five benchmarks; reviewers cite MCB GMS rising from 60.1 for the best baseline to 73.7 with 0.7% invalid outputs.
m72TXFkMUn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results on complex mechanical parts are strong across several benchmarks, with useful same-backbone controls showing the benefit of stepwise generation.
m72TXFkMUn.main_concern: The core idea of execution and visual feedback for CAD programs resembles prior work (Query2CAD, CADReasoner, CADFusion, SOV-CAD), and attribution is not controlled for compute, with per-step execution and rendering overhead not reported.

tf5gd7Ife1.one_liner: Localizes risky steps via the acting agent's own information gain toward unsafe judgments, then applies step-level preference optimization.
tf5gd7Ife1.problem: Trajectory-level safety alignment gives sparse supervision, while step-level alignment usually needs stronger external models to localize risky steps, which adds API cost and privacy risk and may be unavailable for frontier agents.
tf5gd7Ife1.method: AgentFalcon scores each sentence's information gain toward an unsafe judgment elicited from the acting agent, residualizes it against the corresponding safety information gain to find sentences that drive unsafe behavior, intervenes at the earliest risk position, elicits safety reflection, pairs the regenerated safe continuation with the original for preference optimization, and repeats.
tf5gd7Ife1.key_idea: Residualizing a sentence's unsafe-judgment information gain against its safety information gain exposes risk-driving sentences using only the acting model's latent risk awareness.
tf5gd7Ife1.evidence: Four backbones across multiple safety benchmarks (including AgentLAB) and general agentic benchmarks (abstract truncated).
tf5gd7Ife1.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract; reviewers cite AgentLAB attack success rates falling from 57.2, 53.3, 46.0 and 57.2 percent to 9.8, 8.7, 6.9 and 9.9 percent.
tf5gd7Ife1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that self-aware risk localization is a strong idea and that safety improves substantially and consistently across four backbones while task utility is also evaluated.
tf5gd7Ife1.main_concern: Localization depends on the model already recognizing unsafe behavior, and the paper lacks the direct baseline of asking the same model to pick the earliest risky step as well as a comparison of the residualization against simple log-odds.

Cgm5MlLSNs.one_liner: Lifts 2D person features into a canonical 3D voxel space with geometry-semantic attention and reliability-weighted fusion for aerial-ground ReID.
Cgm5MlLSNs.problem: Existing aerial-ground ReID methods learn view-invariant features only in 2D image space, where drastic viewpoint changes keep features coupled to viewpoint bias.
Cgm5MlLSNs.method: VR3D lifts 2D appearance features into a canonical 3D space using 3D priors extracted from single 2D images, then applies 3D Geometry-Semantic Attention between 2D patches and 3D voxels of corresponding body parts based on 3D spatial location. A Reliability-Aware Fusion estimates sample-specific reliability and adaptively aggregates the multi-source representations.
Cgm5MlLSNs.key_idea: Attend between 2D patches and 3D voxels of the same body part by 3D location, then fuse 2D and 3D features with per-sample reliability weights.
Cgm5MlLSNs.evidence: Experiments on CARGO, AG-ReID.v1, and AG-ReID.v2, with ablations on the 3D information, the geometric and semantic terms, and the fusion module (per reviews).
Cgm5MlLSNs.claimed_gains: The abstract excerpt is cut off before its numbers; a reviewer reports CARGO A<->G Rank-1/mAP of 59.38/54.57, which is 5.63/4.93 points above ViSA.
Cgm5MlLSNs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation for moving viewpoint-robust learning into 3D well founded and the experimental results strong, including multi-protocol gains on the three benchmarks.
Cgm5MlLSNs.main_concern: All three reviewers flag the reliance on offline 3D reconstruction (SAM3/SAM3D) whose compute, runtime, and storage cost is not quantified, alongside limited novelty of the attention and fusion modules.

2uKQn4L4oi.one_liner: Diffusion-language-model MLLM that captions multiple image regions in parallel via region prompting and structured attention masking.
2uKQn4L4oi.problem: Autoregressive MLLMs caption multiple regions sequentially, which limits efficiency for region-level perception tasks.
2uKQn4L4oi.method: PerceptionDLM-Base combines a diffusion language model with a visual encoder, and a prompting mechanism then lets the model perceive multiple masked regions at once, generating region descriptions in parallel at sequence and token levels. The authors also build ParaDLC-Bench by extending DLC-Bench with multiple region masks per image.
2uKQn4L4oi.key_idea: Exploit parallel decoding of diffusion language models to caption several masked regions simultaneously, using region prompting and structured attention to avoid cross-region interference.
2uKQn4L4oi.evidence: Region captioning comparisons against diffusion and autoregressive baselines on DLC-Bench and the new ParaDLC-Bench (100 images, per reviews), with ablations on region prompting and structured attention.
2uKQn4L4oi.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract excerpt claims competitive region captioning and significantly better inference efficiency, without figures).
2uKQn4L4oi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and that parallel multi-region decoding gives real wall-clock speedups that grow with the number of regions, supported by ablations.
2uKQn4L4oi.main_concern: Speedups are measured against autoregressive baselines that process regions sequentially, with no batched or joint autoregressive multi-region baseline to show the gain comes from diffusion decoding.

8MGQArMhc9.one_liner: Fine-tunes a video diffusion model for single-step residual regression to refine depth from any source.
8MGQArMhc9.problem: Depth maps from sensors and networks are often low-resolution, noisy, incomplete, inaccurate, or temporally unstable, and existing fixes are task-specific.
8MGQArMhc9.method: RAD formulates depth refinement as residual regression: given an input video and depth map, a fine-tuned video diffusion model makes a single-step residual update to repair the depth. Training uses a curriculum of depth corruptions.
8MGQArMhc9.key_idea: Fine-tune a video diffusion model to predict a single-step residual correction of the input depth, trained on a curriculum of depth corruptions.
8MGQArMhc9.evidence: Depth super-resolution and completion comparisons (including SCRREAM) and refinement of existing depth predictors such as VGGT and pi3, measured on accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency across several datasets (per reviews).
8MGQArMhc9.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims leading depth super-resolution and completion results and better boundary sharpness and temporal stability for existing depth models, without figures).
8MGQArMhc9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a single set of weights that handles many depth sources and error types, with strong completion and super-resolution results and wide evaluation.
8MGQArMhc9.main_concern: Refinement can degrade accurate inputs (for example VGGT-Ω AbsRel rises from 3.21% to 5.25% on TUM-dyn), so gains are not uniform across inputs and metrics.

148eBbNarz.one_liner: Replaces SplineCNN B-spline bases with learnable Padé rational basis functions over pseudo-coordinates in graph convolutions.
148eBbNarz.problem: SplineCNN's B-spline basis count grows exponentially with pseudo-coordinate dimension and relies on sparse activations, making it parameter-inefficient.
148eBbNarz.method: RBF-GNN is a drop-in replacement for SplineCNN layers that uses safe Padé rational functions as the basis over Euclidean, spherical, or angular pseudo-coordinates. Training uses a spline-subspace initialization and a variance-preserving weight rescaling.
148eBbNarz.key_idea: Parametrize the spatial basis of pseudo-coordinate graph convolutions with learnable safe Padé rational functions, initialized from the SplineCNN spline subspace.
148eBbNarz.evidence: Replaces only the SplineCNN layers inside existing architectures and evaluates on eight benchmarks, including semantic keypoint matching, shape matching, and event-camera vision tasks, with multiple seeds (per reviews).
148eBbNarz.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims improved results, or the same accuracy with several times fewer parameters, without figures).
148eBbNarz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a simple drop-in replacement evaluated fairly across diverse benchmarks, with practical parameter efficiency in higher-dimensional settings.
148eBbNarz.main_concern: Much of the gain may come from the SplineCNN-style initialization rather than the Padé basis, since MLP baselines lack a matched initialization and random-initialization results are not tabulated.

H6FXQjTrrX.one_liner: Streams flow-based VLA actions, adapting denoising budget and observation frequency to convergence difficulty with maturity-oriented training.
H6FXQjTrrX.problem: Flow-based VLAs trade latency against quality, and early-released streamed actions must stay reliable while denoising and observation frequency should track per-sample convergence difficulty.
H6FXQjTrrX.method: DASH combines Maturity-Oriented Matching, which improves causal consistency within each action chunk, with Difficulty-Aware Denoising, which jointly adapts denoising budgets and observation frequency to convergence difficulty.
H6FXQjTrrX.key_idea: Train the flow model so early-released actions stay consistent with later denoising (maturity conditioning), and set denoising steps and observation timing from per-sample convergence difficulty.
H6FXQjTrrX.evidence: Simulation (CALVIN) and real-world robot experiments across two backbones and two GPUs, compared with synchronous inference and streaming baselines such as FASTER (per reviews).
H6FXQjTrrX.claimed_gains: Up to 3.44x reaction speedup over synchronous inference and up to 3.26% improvement in average CALVIN success over the strongest streaming baseline.
H6FXQjTrrX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the evaluation broad, with large reductions in denoising computation and reaction time from jointly adapting computation and observation timing.
H6FXQjTrrX.main_concern: Several interacting components give modest individual gains without uncertainty estimates, and reaction-time improvements are mostly estimated from a timing model rather than measured latency.

3AMsGEGlvz.one_liner: Recursive event world model for language-guided multi-camera tracking that propagates association uncertainty through posterior-weighted belief updates.
3AMsGEGlvz.problem: A wrong early match across unobserved gaps corrupts the history used to predict later observations and propagates identity errors across camera handoffs.
3AMsGEGlvz.method: A persistent predictive belief is updated recursively: candidate matches and a temporary null define conditioned target states whose posterior probabilities weight the update. The belief predicts the next camera, arrival time, and entry region, while appearance and language evidence guide association.
3AMsGEGlvz.key_idea: Weight the belief update by posterior probabilities over candidate and null target hypotheses so association uncertainty carries into forecasts of next camera, arrival time, and entry region.
3AMsGEGlvz.evidence: Evaluated on CityFlowV2 and MTMMC, including three-handoff chains, a predictor-matched control against a generic learned updater, and topology-shift experiments.
3AMsGEGlvz.claimed_gains: HOTA of 65.19 on CityFlowV2 and 45.36 on MTMMC; on MTMMC three-handoff chains it preserves identity through all three handoffs in 86.67% of cases versus 76.67% for a similarly sized generic learned updater.
3AMsGEGlvz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a real failure mode, early commitment to a wrong candidate, with a coherent posterior-update design and well-controlled experiments.
3AMsGEGlvz.main_concern: The method depends on a predefined camera graph and topology priors, and performance degrades under unseen topology or misleading language queries.

7cbJEyW0YQ.one_liner: Autoregressive mesh generation that tracks active frontier edges in a Trie with canonical lexicographic keys.
7cbJEyW0YQ.problem: Autoregressive artistic mesh generators represent the current mesh state mainly through sequence history, leaving the active frontier implicit.
7cbJEyW0YQ.method: TrieMesh keeps active frontier edges in a Trie so the next edge to expand is selected deterministically. A shared decoder generates a full face when the frontier is empty and otherwise predicts one completion vertex, reusing the two known endpoints of the active edge.
7cbJEyW0YQ.key_idea: Store frontier edges in a Trie under canonical lexicographic keys for deterministic next-edge selection, and predict only the completion vertex of each active edge.
7cbJEyW0YQ.evidence: Geometric-fidelity comparisons with recent autoregressive baselines under comparable token budgets, plus a mesh hole-filling extension.
7cbJEyW0YQ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims improved geometric fidelity over recent autoregressive baselines under comparable token budgets, without figures).
7cbJEyW0YQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see explicit frontier modeling as an interesting extension of FACE that reduces token count and extends to mesh hole filling.
7cbJEyW0YQ.main_concern: There is no direct comparison with FACE, the closest baseline, and the contribution looks incremental over it.

2Ql5mfYaVv.one_liner: Fully homomorphic speculative decoding that packs candidate tokens into shared ciphertexts for private LLM inference.
2Ql5mfYaVv.problem: FHE is inefficient for autoregressive decoding, which emits one token at a time, while speculative decoding's sampling, verification, and commit steps are expensive to realize under FHE.
2Ql5mfYaVv.method: Taurus packs many speculative candidate tokens so expensive FHE computation is shared across token states. It adds a homomorphic sampling protocol that avoids scanning the full vocabulary with encrypted comparisons, a private verification protocol without encrypted division or data-dependent branching, and FixedTraceCommit for writing accepted tokens and KV states.
2Ql5mfYaVv.key_idea: Pack speculative candidates into ciphertexts, sample hierarchically over packed vocabularies, and verify acceptance by replacing division with multiplication, so each target forward serves many tokens.
2Ql5mfYaVv.evidence: End-to-end decoding and ablations of the sampling, verification, and commit steps across mathematical reasoning, dialogue, and code generation, with comparison to CacheMir at context length 256 (per reviews).
2Ql5mfYaVv.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract excerpt is cut off before any results).
2Ql5mfYaVv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find packing speculative candidates into ciphertexts a good observation, with efficient hierarchical sampling and a complete encrypted sampling, verification, and KV-cache pipeline.
2Ql5mfYaVv.main_concern: The end-to-end evaluation is sparse: one draft model, context length 256, and no ablation isolating the benefit of packing candidates.

JOga6weLRW.one_liner: Average-cost actor-critic that keeps each policy update inside a graded certificate guaranteeing moment and mixing regularity for future learning.
JOga6weLRW.problem: In continuing tasks with unbounded states, an approximate policy update can make the on-policy process heavy-tailed or poorly mixed, making later value estimates and gradients unreliable.
JOga6weLRW.method: SVPO builds a graded certificate into the learned policy so each update preserves the statistical conditions needed by subsequent learning, while retaining the physical task cost. The same construction yields Tilt, a certificate-preserving correction for existing policy optimizers.
JOga6weLRW.key_idea: Enforce a graded stability certificate in the learned policy itself so every update preserves the moment bounds and mixing needed by the next actor-critic step.
JOga6weLRW.evidence: Proofs of moment and mixing guarantees along the adaptive policy sequence and almost-sure convergence to projected stationarity under standard assumptions; experiments on switched LTI and input-saturated systems and, per reviews, queuing problems.
JOga6weLRW.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims almost-sure convergence to projected stationarity under standard assumptions, not numeric gains).
JOga6weLRW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that policy updates breaking future learning in unbounded-state continuing RL is an important problem and that the certificate construction is coherent and useful.
JOga6weLRW.main_concern: The convergence guarantee is conditional on assumptions the certificate does not imply, such as the actor field being the gradient of some F and a TD-dynamics condition.

dZQ6ga61X3.one_liner: Language-model preference models rank candidate ML solutions so research agents spend limited execution budget on promising ones.
dZQ6ga61X3.problem: AI research agents can propose far more candidates than they can afford to evaluate, since a single evaluation can consume days of GPU time.
dZQ6ga61X3.method: Two RPM variants are built from pretrained language models: an inference-only model that reasons over candidate plans, code, and previously executed solutions, and an agentic model that also runs small-scale pilot experiments. Both are integrated into the AIRA-dojo research agent.
dZQ6ga61X3.key_idea: Rank unexecuted candidate solutions with a pretrained LM conditioned on the live search history, optionally running small pilot experiments, to allocate the execution budget.
dZQ6ga61X3.evidence: AIRA-dojo on AIRS-Bench with four LLM backbones (GPT-5, Gemma 4-31B, Qwen3.6-27B, Muse Glimmer), plus offline experiments on context size, candidate pool size, and pilot budgets (per reviews).
dZQ6ga61X3.claimed_gains: Both variants improve the average normalized score over the unguided agent across four backbones, matching its 24-hour performance in roughly 14 hours with less than 60% of its execution budget.
dZQ6ga61X3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and well motivated, and that RPMs match the unguided baseline with a fraction of the compute.
dZQ6ga61X3.main_concern: Gains are modest and comparisons are thin: random choice is the only end-to-end baseline, with no static-judge baseline and limited novelty over existing judge-based candidate selection.

ReTMEWVKMp.one_liner: Proves that a winner-take-all bottleneck in multi-task networks recovers categorical latent factors as a structured permutation.
ReTMEWVKMp.problem: How winner-take-all bottlenecks extract categorical latent factors from highly non-linearly entangled data has remained unclear.
ReTMEWVKMp.method: A winner-take-all (WTA) bottleneck inside a deep network is trained on multiple tasks over categorical latent factors. A theorem shows that when the WTA structure matches the latent-factor structure and all tasks are solved perfectly, the learned representation is a structured permutation of the latents; mismatched structures are tested empirically on two datasets.
ReTMEWVKMp.key_idea: Place a winner-take-all layer whose structure matches the categorical latent factors before the multi-task heads, so near-optimal multi-task training forces a symbolic, permuted latent code.
ReTMEWVKMp.evidence: A proof under stated conditions, empirical tests on two datasets with mismatched WTA structure, and an evaluation of the generalization behavior of the acquired symbolic representations.
ReTMEWVKMp.claimed_gains: not stated (theoretical result; the abstract gives no numeric gains).
ReTMEWVKMp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the link between biological WTA circuits and disentangled representation learning interesting, and the identifiability result for categorical latents exact and checkable.
ReTMEWVKMp.main_concern: The theory needs strong assumptions (known latent-factor structure, informative tasks, perfect task performance), and application to real data is unclear because the number of factors and categories is usually unknown.

zXf2G519g2.one_liner: Feed-forward full-head Gaussian avatar reconstruction from few portraits, with identity anchoring and adversarial domain alignment for mobile animation.
zXf2G519g2.problem: Joint avatar-motion learning and mixed-source training suffer representation confounding, where identity leaks into expression components and canonical features encode dataset-level acquisition attributes.
zXf2G519g2.method: A feed-forward network jointly estimates motion and predicts an explicit mesh-bound Gaussian avatar, using Neutral Identity Anchoring to limit identity leakage into expression and Adversarial Domain Alignment to discourage dataset attributes in canonical features. The asset stores identity-adapted mesh blendshapes and Gaussian appearance bases, so animation is basis mixing without per-frame neural decoding.
zXf2G519g2.key_idea: Anchor identity with zero-expression renderings and adversarially remove dataset attributes from canonical features, then animate by mixing precomputed mesh blendshapes and Gaussian appearance bases.
zXf2G519g2.evidence: Experiments on VFHQ, AVA256, and RenderMe-360 including a public-data-only training variant, plus throughput tests on two mobile devices.
zXf2G519g2.claimed_gains: Above 60 FPS for four concurrent avatars on a shared 1024x1024 canvas on both tested mobile devices, given precomputed driving controls; reconstruction and identity gains are not quantified in the abstract.
zXf2G519g2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a protocol-matched evaluation across three datasets, a public-data variant that reduces concerns about data advantage, and efficient mobile rendering.
zXf2G519g2.main_concern: Novelty is incremental and it is unclear what drives the gains, since the identity-anchoring and domain-alignment designs are standard and most ablations show small differences.

Gzda5HNz7Y.one_liner: Learns an adapter that evolves task-specific LLM agent harnesses from few examples, transferring the evolution strategy across tasks.
Gzda5HNz7Y.problem: Existing harness evolution methods optimize a task-specific harness from scratch for each new task, needing substantial task-specific data and evolution steps.
Gzda5HNz7Y.method: ReHarness learns a transferable evolution strategy from multiple offline tasks and applies it to adapt task-specific worker harnesses to new tasks using a few examples. Per reviews, an adapter harness is optimized across tasks offline and then frozen at deployment.
Gzda5HNz7Y.key_idea: Optimize an adapter that edits worker harnesses across multiple offline tasks, then freeze it so a new task needs only a few examples to evolve its harness.
Gzda5HNz7Y.evidence: Four LLMs and six benchmarks, with gains on four unseen tasks and a comparison with Self-Harness on two offline-suite tasks under the same data budget; ablations on five-shot, initial adapter, and history (per reviews).
Gzda5HNz7Y.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims consistent gains on four new tasks and better results than Self-Harness on two offline tasks under the same data budget, without figures).
Gzda5HNz7Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusable structure in harness evolution is an interesting observation, and that the offline-adapter then frozen-deployment design is coherent with consistent gains across model-benchmark pairs.
Gzda5HNz7Y.main_concern: Comparisons are thin, with no cross-task baseline such as Hyperagents or a strong few-shot adaptation baseline, and unexplained low base scores (for example 26.7% on SWE-bench Verified) may inflate the gains.

NLQtGgzNwn.one_liner: Recovers sparse-attention LLMs by distilling the dense checkpoint's token distributions on trajectories sampled from the sparse student.
NLQtGgzNwn.problem: Sparse attention cuts inference cost but can cause sparse reasoning drift, where early token deviations compound through autoregressive feedback, degrading reasoning and prolonging generation.
NLQtGgzNwn.method: SparseOPD uses the original dense checkpoint as a privileged teacher to supervise next-token distributions on trajectories generated by the evolving sparse student. LowP-40 supervises only the lowest-probability 40% of tokens.
NLQtGgzNwn.key_idea: Distill the dense model's next-token distributions on the sparse student's own rollouts, so training covers the states actually reached under sparse decoding.
NLQtGgzNwn.evidence: Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-14B, and Ministral-3-14B on mathematical reasoning (including AIME 2026 and HMMT) and code generation, against cross-entropy recovery and fixed-trajectory distillation.
NLQtGgzNwn.claimed_gains: On AIME 2026 it nearly restores dense accuracy on Qwen3-4B and exceeds it on Qwen3-14B, keeps a 1.73x request-level speedup over dense on Qwen3-4B HMMT, and LowP-40 matches full-token recovery quality while speeding end-to-end training by 1.19x.
NLQtGgzNwn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the approach simple and the prefill/decode diagnosis of sparse degradation useful, with large gains over cross-entropy recovery and Qwen results close to dense.
NLQtGgzNwn.main_concern: The gain of on-policy distillation over fixed-trajectory distillation is sometimes small relative to benchmark noise, with no seed variance or confidence intervals on 30-problem sets.

1Wza4JL7TQ.one_liner: Steers LLM activations by hyperspherical rotation toward an optimal-transport-weighted truthful prototype with task-aware von Mises-Fisher gating.
1Wza4JL7TQ.problem: Training-free hyperspherical steering has noise-sensitive uniform centroids, a single-difference prototype whose antipodal constraint biases rotation direction, and global parameters that fit neither discriminative nor generative tasks.
1Wza4JL7TQ.method: Offline, prototypes are built with hyperspherical optimal transport weighting and an independent dual-prototype setup removes the antipodal constraint, using the truthful prototype as the correction anchor. Online, a task-aware von Mises-Fisher gate regulates intervention strength.
1Wza4JL7TQ.key_idea: Weight class centroids by hyperspherical optimal transport, rotate toward an independent truthful prototype instead of an antipodal one, and gate strength with a task-aware von Mises-Fisher mechanism.
1Wza4JL7TQ.evidence: LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B on six benchmarks (TruthfulQA, COPA, StoryCloze, MMLU, WinoGrande, BoolQ), with ablations against single-prototype variants and a representation rank-collapse analysis (per reviews).
1Wza4JL7TQ.claimed_gains: Average improvements of 5.33% on multiple-choice tasks and 10.14% on open-ended generation over baselines, with negligible extra computational overhead.
1Wza4JL7TQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method gives consistent gains over spherical steering across six benchmarks and two models with small added latency (2.15% for multiple choice, 0.56% for open-ended generation).
1Wza4JL7TQ.main_concern: The source of the gains is unclear: the OT weighting lacks justification, the task-aware gate relies on manually grid-searched alpha and beta per task category, and Theorem 2 is stated too strongly.

t4j8ZQwcZP.one_liner: Synthesizes executable agent tasks and environments from skills using difficulty patterns, task blueprints, and iterative task hardening.
t4j8ZQwcZP.problem: Building executable tasks with complete environments for agent post-training is hard to scale, and a skill alone lacks the detail of a challenging concrete task.
t4j8ZQwcZP.method: Skill2Env maps agent capability demands to reusable difficulty patterns, instantiates them as task blueprints (objectives, challenges, environment facts, information boundaries, acceptance criteria), and builds task instructions, execution substrates, workspaces, and rubric-based evaluators from them. Iterative Task Hardening uses solver execution evidence to strengthen weak task designs and revise blueprints and environments.
t4j8ZQwcZP.key_idea: Turn each skill into a task blueprint from reusable difficulty patterns, then harden tasks using solver execution evidence that flags insufficiently challenging designs.
t4j8ZQwcZP.evidence: Supervised fine-tuning on 1.5K high-scoring trajectories from Skill2Env environments, with improvements reported on seven benchmarks and four Terminal-Bench harnesses and nearly three thousand executable tasks built (per reviews).
t4j8ZQwcZP.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract excerpt reports consistent improvements after fine-tuning on 1.5K trajectories but is cut off before figures).
t4j8ZQwcZP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decomposition of agent capability demands into 100 difficulty patterns and a unified task blueprint useful, with training benefits across multiple benchmarks and agent harnesses.
t4j8ZQwcZP.main_concern: No controlled comparison separates the framework from the strong teacher model, for example the same model generating tasks directly from skills or other synthesis methods under the same budget.

GNaSBCauko.one_liner: Jointly optimizes prompts and workflows to build reusable symbolic regression agents that wrap PySR or an LLM equation generator.
GNaSBCauko.problem: LLM-based symbolic regression systems rely on manually designed workflows and prompts, although the agent harness shapes search priors and how numerical feedback guides equation refinement.
GNaSBCauko.method: HarnessSR first optimizes role prompts using equation-discovery feedback in basic workflows, then jointly searches prompt assignments and workflows with brief adaptation, and finally refines role instructions by reflecting on residual patterns, candidate structures, and search outcomes. It supports either PySR or an LLM equation generator through tool-specific interfaces.
GNaSBCauko.key_idea: Treat the SR agent harness as an optimization target, searching prompts and workflows with equation-discovery feedback, then refining role instructions by reflection on residuals.
GNaSBCauko.evidence: LSR-Synth in LLM-SRBench across three backbones, with in-distribution and out-of-distribution accuracy comparisons against baselines such as SR-Scientist and PySR (per reviews).
GNaSBCauko.claimed_gains: Mean ID Acc0.01 of 61.33% across three backbones, a 45.0% relative improvement over the next-best baseline.
GNaSBCauko.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating the agent harness as an optimization target is a useful reframing and that accuracy improves across all three evaluated backbones.
GNaSBCauko.main_concern: Search budgets are unmatched (13 PySR calls per task versus one for the PySR baseline), so gains may reflect extra search rather than better guidance.

vtUtyM2V5z.one_liner: Recovers a rigged, re-poseable asset from a single posed mesh via diffusion-predicted paired skeletons and sparse skinning.
vtUtyM2V5z.problem: Existing rigging and skinning methods assume rest-pose inputs or evaluate skeletons and weights separately, leaving recovery of a complete animation-ready asset from a single posed mesh unsolved.
vtUtyM2V5z.method: AniRig conditions on a semantic hierarchy (joint names and parent-child links, user-given or inferred by a VLM from rendered views), predicts observed and rest skeletons jointly in one diffusion model, and estimates structured sparse skinning weights over a compact set of candidate joints. A differentiable pose-to-rest construction recovers the canonical rest mesh and enables coupled fine-tuning with asset-level surface supervision.
vtUtyM2V5z.key_idea: Predict paired observed and rest skeletons in one hierarchy-conditioned diffusion model and couple them with sparse skinning through a differentiable pose-to-rest construction.
vtUtyM2V5z.evidence: Articulation-XL2.0 evaluation of skeleton and skinning accuracy, plus ablations on paired skeleton modeling and asset-level fine-tuning measuring rest-mesh Chamfer distance and re-posing (per reviews).
vtUtyM2V5z.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract excerpt says only that AniRig improves skeleton and skinning weight accuracy on Articulation-XL2.0 and is cut off before figures).
vtUtyM2V5z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the task practically valuable and the joint modeling of skeletons, skinning, and pose-to-rest recovery well motivated, with supporting ablations.
vtUtyM2V5z.main_concern: Complete-asset recovery is validated mainly against the method's own ablations, with no independent pose-to-rest comparison and limited testing of inferred hierarchies on hard articulated cases.

18FC15e2TV.one_liner: Adapts video generation backbones to whole-body mesh recovery by predicting shaded canonical-color renderings and gating local joint evidence.
18FC15e2TV.problem: Video generation priors focus on visual synthesis, leaving a gap to the explicit human geometry needed for body and hand mesh recovery under occlusion and partial visibility.
18FC15e2TV.method: DreamHMR follows a global-to-local strategy: Global Body Representation Transfer trains the video backbone to predict complete human renderings to learn surface correspondence and posed geometry, then Local Joint Feature Enhancement combines contextual estimates with reliable local evidence to refine body and hand detail while limiting interference from occluders and background.
18FC15e2TV.key_idea: Fine-tune a video backbone to render the complete human with canonical coloring and shading, then refine joints from locally sampled features gated by support scores.
18FC15e2TV.evidence: Experiments on five datasets with four video backbones, including 3DPW, EMDB-1, and RICH, plus occlusion tests and ablations on rendering targets and local enhancement (per reviews).
18FC15e2TV.claimed_gains: The abstract excerpt claims the best model outperforms existing methods on all reported 3DPW metrics but is cut off before figures; a reviewer cites occlusion body/hand MPJPE falling from 120.0/68.4 to 106.3/57.8 mm with canonical coloring plus shading versus RGB supervision.
18FC15e2TV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like adapting video-generation representations to human mesh recovery, with a clear global-to-local motivation and strong results across benchmarks and backbones backed by informative ablations.
18FC15e2TV.main_concern: The occlusion evaluation uses artificial rectangular masks rather than natural occluders, so the occlusion-robustness claim is narrower than motivated and cross-method attribution is partly confounded.

5ScSgBVWzn.one_liner: Repurposes a pretrained video generator as a feed-forward 4D perceiver with a single encoder pass and query-based cross-attention decoder.
5ScSgBVWzn.problem: Unified recovery of 4D geometry and motion from monocular video is needed, and it is unclear whether a pretrained video generator can serve as a feed-forward perceiver without iterative denoising.
5ScSgBVWzn.method: Gen4P encodes clean video latents in a single pass and predicts requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder using on-demand spatial queries and continuous-time queries. A pretrained video-depth LoRA is plugged in as a frozen geometry prior with no extra trainable parameters.
5ScSgBVWzn.key_idea: Encode clean video latents once, then decode any requested 4D attribute with spatial and continuous-time queries, adding a frozen depth LoRA as a geometry prior.
5ScSgBVWzn.evidence: 3D point tracking, video depth, and camera pose estimation, including unseen dynamic benchmarks such as PStudio and Sintel, plus noise-level and Depth-LoRA studies and qualitative in-the-wild videos.
5ScSgBVWzn.claimed_gains: The abstract claims top or competitive performance on 3D point tracking, video depth, and camera pose estimation without numbers; a reviewer cites PStudio tracking APD of 82.11 vs 79.61 and Sintel AbsRel of 0.182 vs 0.200 for the second model variant.
5ScSgBVWzn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining video-generation features with a query-based decoder is effective, with strong results on unseen dynamic benchmarks and good preservation of thin structures.
5ScSgBVWzn.main_concern: The central claim that video generators are 4D perceivers is not isolated by controlled comparisons, since the generator prior is not separated from the 200K-clip training mix or from alternative pretrained encoders.

d943RAfDAV.one_liner: Unlearns LLM knowledge by relocating suppressed token probability to reference-branch anchor tokens with an InfoNCE-like loss.
d943RAfDAV.problem: Suppression-based unlearning pushes probability mass toward the model's original top-k preferences because softmax normalization redistributes it, so forgotten knowledge can resurface through similar expressions.
d943RAfDAV.method: SAR builds a dynamic reference-branch token set and a current-model token set at each answer position, then uses an InfoNCE-like loss to relocate probability toward reference-defined anchors.
d943RAfDAV.key_idea: At each answer position, pull probability mass from suppressed tokens toward tokens preferred only by a reference branch, using an InfoNCE-like loss.
d943RAfDAV.evidence: A diagnostic analysis across five baselines, theoretical analysis of local logit updates, and experiments on TOFU and MUSE News with Llama-3.2-1B/3B and Llama-2-7B (per reviews).
d943RAfDAV.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says theory and experiments on diverse benchmarks confirm effectiveness, without numbers).
d943RAfDAV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation compelling, since suppressing a response does not say where the displaced probability goes, and the method simple with a clear mathematical basis.
d943RAfDAV.main_concern: Nothing establishes that reference-only anchor tokens are semantically safe, since the reference model may still hold the forgotten knowledge.

MF4OgCxWV6.one_liner: World model whose latent makes actions act linearly with the target at the origin, giving a closed-form optimal policy.
MF4OgCxWV6.problem: World models trained to predict can leave the planner without a route to the target when tasks demand precision, because the prediction and planning objectives come apart.
MF4OgCxWV6.method: Action-coordinate world models learn latent representations in which actions act linearly and the target sits at the origin, moving structure from the planner into the representation. Theory gives conditions for existence and learnability from high-dimensional observations, plus a closed-form policy with optimality conditions.
MF4OgCxWV6.key_idea: Learn latent action-coordinates where actions are linear and the target is the origin, so the optimal action comes from a closed-form linear solve rather than a planner.
MF4OgCxWV6.evidence: Theory on existence, structure, and learnability of action-coordinates, and experiments on high-fidelity visually observed benchmarks against planner-based and gradient-based world models and offline RL, with assumption-breaking ablations (per reviews).
MF4OgCxWV6.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says action-coordinate world models outperform planner-based and gradient-based world models, without numbers).
MF4OgCxWV6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory and architecture fit together, since moving structure into the representation turns planning into a linear solve, and the assumption ablations broadly follow the theory.
MF4OgCxWV6.main_concern: Main results use data anchored at the true per-context optimum (a privileged calibration assumption), and the world-model baselines are weak or trained under different configurations.

Gd1n5T6KD1.one_liner: Scalable anchor-based multi-view clustering that couples sample-anchor representations with a spectrally regularized adaptive anchor topology.
Gd1n5T6KD1.problem: Existing anchor-based multi-view clustering emphasizes consistency without enough cluster discriminability and treats representation learning and topology optimization as separate processes.
Gd1n5T6KD1.method: CORE learns view-specific sample-anchor representations through robust reconstruction, with a low-rank tensor structure capturing high-order cross-view consistency. An adaptive anchor topology is inferred from the refined representations and regularized by spectral connectivity constraints, so representation and topology refine each other.
Gd1n5T6KD1.key_idea: Jointly optimize tensor-regularized sample-anchor representations and a spectrally constrained anchor topology so each refines the other.
Gd1n5T6KD1.evidence: not stated (the abstract excerpt gives no datasets or settings; reviews mention a qualitative visualization of the learned anchor topology and anchor-count selection from a preset candidate set).
Gd1n5T6KD1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coupling of sample-anchor representation learning with a cluster-aware anchor topology is coherent, and that the anchor-level graph keeps cost manageable without sample-wise graphs.
Gd1n5T6KD1.main_concern: The added benefit of coupling the components and the quality of the learned anchor topology are not quantitatively analyzed, since the topology is shown only qualitatively.

cQkSamYGQi.one_liner: Selects parents in self-improving agent archives with EXP3 and best-arm identification to avoid collapse onto one lineage.
cQkSamYGQi.problem: In archive-based self-improving agents, parent selection can repeatedly favor closely related agents (genetic homogenization), leaving alternative designs few chances to produce descendants.
cQkSamYGQi.method: WGM selects parents with an EXP3-based rule that combines clade statistics with a uniform exploration floor, and uses best arm identification to allocate extra evaluations and pick the final agent. The paper proves Thompson-sampling selection concentrates reproduction on one lineage, while WGM gives every lineage a polynomially growing expected number of expansions.
cQkSamYGQi.key_idea: Replace Thompson-sampling parent selection with EXP3 over clade statistics plus a uniform exploration floor, then use best arm identification to spend evaluations and choose the final agent.
cQkSamYGQi.evidence: Proofs on Thompson-sampling concentration and WGM lineage expansion, plus experiments on SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot under matched evaluation budgets, with transfer to held-out coding tasks and ablations of the two components (per reviews).
cQkSamYGQi.claimed_gains: WGM discovers agents that outperform prior methods on SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot under matched evaluation budgets; a reviewer reports margins of 3.3 points over HGM on SWE-Verified-60 and 4.5 points on Polyglot.
cQkSamYGQi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework simple and interpretable, with each of its two components improving results in the ablation.
cQkSamYGQi.main_concern: The main comparison is narrow (only DGM and HGM on SWE-Verified-60 and Polyglot) and key parameters such as the exploration share are fixed without analysis.

IhddmioLtO.one_liner: Debiases prior-data fitted networks with efficient-influence-function label and prior corrections to speed posterior concentration for semi-parametric targets.
IhddmioLtO.problem: Even a Bayes-optimal idealized PFN can have a posterior concentration rate that depends on nuisance-function rates and slows as the prior becomes more diverse.
IhddmioLtO.method: Two debiasing strategies based on efficient influence functions are introduced: a label correction applied to training labels and a prior correction. Theory shows the debiased PFNs' concentration rates asymptotically match frequentist bias-corrected estimators.
IhddmioLtO.key_idea: Build the efficient-influence-function bias correction into PFN pretraining, by correcting synthetic training labels or the prior, so posterior concentration matches debiased frequentist estimators.
IhddmioLtO.evidence: Theorems on posterior concentration, Bernstein-von Mises, and minimax optimality, plus synthetic experiments comparing standard and debiased PFNs for the average treatment effect on one prior (per reviews).
IhddmioLtO.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract gives theoretical guarantees: concentration rates matching frequentist bias-corrected estimators, with Bernstein-von Mises and minimax optimality under additional assumptions).
IhddmioLtO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the link between amortized Bayesian inference with PFNs and semi-parametric efficiency theory valuable, and building the correction into pretraining labels appealing.
IhddmioLtO.main_concern: The theoretical results rest on extra appendix assumptions that largely assume the conclusions, and experiments are limited to one synthetic prior without frequentist debiased baselines.

PWhhcMpmW5.one_liner: Predicts RNA-ligand interactions by ranking surrogate conformers, keeping the top two via sparse posterior, with physics-informed screened-residual regularization.
PWhhcMpmW5.problem: Single-state RNA-ligand models collapse multiple conformational states into one static representation, blurring state-specific interaction signals when high-resolution tertiary-structure supervision is scarce.
PWhhcMpmW5.method: PIPER represents each RNA-ligand pair as a compact set of surrogate conformers built with coordinate charts as inductive biases, ranks them with prior guidance and sparse residue-atom interactions, retains the two highest-utility conformers via a Top-2 posterior, and aggregates their scores. A source-aware screened residual regularizes the local RNA-ligand interaction.
PWhhcMpmW5.key_idea: Let a small set of surrogate conformers compete via prior-guided ranking, keep the top two with a sparse posterior, and regularize local interactions with a screened residual.
PWhhcMpmW5.evidence: Three benchmarks with several distribution-shift protocols including RNA cold-start, and ablations on conformer count (Top-1, Top-2, All-3) and the regularizer (per reviews).
PWhhcMpmW5.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract excerpt is cut off before any results).
PWhhcMpmW5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multi-conformer hypothesis clear and testable, with evaluation across multiple datasets and distribution shifts and ablations supporting the key components.
PWhhcMpmW5.main_concern: The surrogate conformers are not validated against real RNA structures, so the multi-conformer reasoning claim outruns the evidence.

pEFaHlmGni.one_liner: Training-free streaming video QA that retrieves KV-cache evidence as event skeletons using query-specific attention heads and interaction memory.
pEFaHlmGni.problem: KV-cache streaming video methods store memory as independent visual tokens, ignoring temporal semantics and giving fragmented retrieval that misses continuous evidence.
pEFaHlmGni.method: Event-ReHead keeps frame-level retrieval but reorganizes retrieved evidence into a compact event skeleton, selects query-specific attention heads to build more discriminative retrieval representations, and adds a lightweight interaction memory that selectively reuses prior question-answer context.
pEFaHlmGni.key_idea: Reorganize retrieved KV-cache frames into an event skeleton capturing temporal structure, select attention heads per query for retrieval, and reuse prior question-answer context as memory.
pEFaHlmGni.evidence: Four streaming and three offline benchmarks across diverse VLM backbones, with GPU memory and time-to-first-token analysis (per reviews).
pEFaHlmGni.claimed_gains: Up to +4.1% gains in streaming settings; the rest of the abstract excerpt is cut off.
pEFaHlmGni.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation sound and the results consistent across benchmarks, with stable GPU memory as video length grows and no backbone training needed.
pEFaHlmGni.main_concern: The event-granularity and top-K head-selection choices lack justification and comparison with memory-based methods such as ReKV, and one reviewer found score inconsistencies between the text and tables.

gC7iUKnQSb.one_liner: Benchmark testing whether agent memory systems obey user instructions to not store, forget, or withhold information.
gC7iUKnQSb.problem: Memory work focuses on retention and personalization, assuming everything should be memorized, while users in real ChatGPT conversations explicitly ask for information to be removed or disregarded.
gC7iUKnQSb.method: MemCtrl is a benchmark with three settings: Incognito (do not store newly disclosed information), Forget (remove stored information), and Withhold (temporarily disregard stored information). It uses recall and application probes to evaluate six memory systems and two production chatbots, then traces memory operations to locate failures.
gC7iUKnQSb.key_idea: Define three memory-control instruction types, probe both recall and downstream application, and trace memory operations to localize where control fails.
gC7iUKnQSb.evidence: Evaluation of six memory systems plus ChatGPT and Claude across the Incognito, Forget, and Withhold settings, with phase-wise and operation-level failure analysis.
gC7iUKnQSb.claimed_gains: No system reliably follows all three instruction types; ChatGPT and Claude surface restricted information in 39.4%-64.7% of controlled cases on average.
gC7iUKnQSb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets an overlooked, real user-facing problem, with a useful Incognito, Forget, and Withhold distinction and diagnostics beyond aggregate scores.
gC7iUKnQSb.main_concern: Evaluation validity is questionable: production chatbots are tested by browser automation without a reproducible toolkit, and systems lacking a control interface fail by construction.

jBlNOcywem.one_liner: Builds a relativizing multi-prover interactive proof for scalable oversight, using isolated or rewound copies of one AI model.
jBlNOcywem.problem: Debate is efficient but assumes one of two provers is truthful, while single-prover relativizing proofs drop that assumption at substantially greater computational cost.
jBlNOcywem.method: The paper constructs a relativizing MIP for computations whose outputs are robust to changing a small fraction of oracle answers, using two provers that may coordinate beforehand but cannot communicate during verification. The separation is realized with isolated copies of an AI model or by rewinding one model to a prior state.
jBlNOcywem.key_idea: Use two non-communicating provers, realized by isolated model copies or by rewinding one model's state, to verify oracle-aided computations without assuming any prover is truthful.
jBlNOcywem.evidence: A theoretical construction with guarantees for epsilon-robust oracle computations, plus a small MNIST verification experiment (per reviews).
jBlNOcywem.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract excerpt says honest provers run in nearly the time of the original computation, without further figures).
jBlNOcywem.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the observation that prover isolation is cheap for AI models interesting, and removing the honest-prover assumption while keeping soundness a strong, clean, modular result.
jBlNOcywem.main_concern: There is a gap between motivation and results: the theory covers epsilon-robust oracle circuits, and the only experiment (an MNIST majority vote) is close to a trivial no-prover baseline.

W1asQ8L4D5.one_liner: Federated LSVI-UCB using determinant-triggered synchronization and stepwise backward updates that share only compressed sufficient statistics.
W1asQ8L4D5.problem: Multi-agent RL with linear function approximation typically shares raw trajectories, so communication scales linearly with episodes and conflicts with federated privacy constraints.
W1asQ8L4D5.method: Fed-LSVI synchronizes agents when a determinant-based event trigger fires and uses a stepwise backward update so agents exchange only compressed sufficient statistics instead of raw trajectories.
W1asQ8L4D5.key_idea: Trigger synchronization by a determinant condition and recompute regression targets backward step by step from broadcast value estimates, so only sufficient statistics are exchanged.
W1asQ8L4D5.evidence: Regret and communication-cost proofs for episodic MDPs with linear function approximation (homogeneous and heterogeneous environments per reviews), plus small synthetic experiments in the appendix.
W1asQ8L4D5.claimed_gains: Regret bound of O~(sqrt(M d^3 H^4 T)) matching the best-known multi-agent bound for linear function approximation, with communication cost growing only logarithmically in T.
W1asQ8L4D5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the backward synchronization protocol addresses a real obstacle to statistics-only communication and that the analysis gives joint regret and logarithmic-communication guarantees.
W1asQ8L4D5.main_concern: Novelty over existing low-switching LSVI methods is unclear, and the experiments are small synthetic runs without competing methods or synchronization ablations.

KKXY4FEKLp.one_liner: Training-free concept bottleneck for remote sensing using greedy quadtree routing and MLLM-based concept scores blended across scales.
KKXY4FEKLp.problem: Concept-bottleneck models for remote sensing are either too expensive to train or perform poorly without annotation, and training-free versions need fine detail in both image and concept space.
KKXY4FEKLp.method: APERTURE locates small concepts by greedy quadtree routing over image scales, replaces contrastive vision-language models with pretrained MLLMs that give reliable concept scores, and blends scores at the global image and native concept-scale levels.
KKXY4FEKLp.key_idea: Route concept queries to the image scale where each concept appears via greedy quadtree search, score them with an MLLM, and blend global and native-scale scores.
KKXY4FEKLp.evidence: SiFC, a new fine-grained concept-centric dataset across three countries with human-reviewed class-level concept maps (800 images and six facility classes per a reviewer), plus component-removal tests and temporal descriptor-update experiments.
KKXY4FEKLp.claimed_gains: On SiFC, APERTURE outperforms the best training-free baselines by more than 10 percentage points in macro F1-score and also outperforms supervised concept bottleneck models.
KKXY4FEKLp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical and the combination of global context with concept-specific local views intuitive and training-free, with experiments across several MLLM backbones and baselines.
KKXY4FEKLp.main_concern: The multiscale routing adds little (macro-F1 of 80.19% versus 78.62% for global-only, and barely above fixed-scale cropping), and the contributions of individual components are not disentangled.

8cyuL4cD8E.one_liner: Co-evolves a small SQL injection detector with an LLM attacker that synthesizes schema-grounded examples from verifier feedback.
8cyuL4cD8E.problem: Small local SQLi detectors trained once on a fixed corpus cannot absorb new variants without full retraining and spend budget on already-learned patterns while underrepresented variants with unresolved errors get little.
8cyuL4cD8E.method: In each round an Attacker synthesizes SQLi examples guided by Verifier signals on which injection clusters need more training budget and where to explore variants; the Defender fine-tunes on the resulting slice, and its errors on a fixed validation set become the next round's Verifier feedback.
8cyuL4cD8E.key_idea: Couple attack synthesis and detector fine-tuning in rounds, with verifier-derived error clusters directing both training budget and variant exploration toward the detector's current weaknesses.
8cyuL4cD8E.evidence: Experiments on SQLI-BENCH with database, query, and payload-template splits (four, two, and five databases for train, validation, and test), ablations of the feedback components, and an expert audit of a test subset (per reviews).
8cyuL4cD8E.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract excerpt is cut off before results).
8cyuL4cD8E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the careful splits that separate databases, queries, and payload templates, a reasonable error-guided training idea, and ablations that explain the contribution of feedback.
8cyuL4cD8E.main_concern: Methodological novelty over existing feedback-guided attack generation and adversarial retraining (WAF-A-MoLE, ModSec-AdvLearn, SqliGPT) is unclear, with no comparison to these nearest neighbors.

QgFykzzb4A.one_liner: Reallocates a fixed rollout budget across prompts to equalize MaxRL's finite-rollout gradient attenuation factors.
QgFykzzb4A.problem: Under finite rollouts, MaxRL attenuates each prompt's likelihood gradient by a factor that depends on its success probability and rollout count, so uniform allocation over-attenuates low-success prompts and distorts their relative contributions.
QgFykzzb4A.method: SERA formulates rollout allocation as a fixed-budget max-min problem, derives a waterline solution to its continuous relaxation, and adds a multiplicity correction that removes the extra prompt weighting caused by heterogeneous rollout counts.
QgFykzzb4A.key_idea: Allocate rollouts per prompt by a max-min waterline solution so finite-rollout scaling factors are approximately equal, with a multiplicity correction for unequal rollout counts.
QgFykzzb4A.evidence: A controlled ImageNet setting measuring alignment with exact likelihood gradients, and maze navigation and mathematical reasoning under matched training rollout budgets.
QgFykzzb4A.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims stronger alignment with exact likelihood gradients and improved multi-sample solution coverage over MaxRL under matched budgets, without figures).
QgFykzzb4A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the insight well motivated, the allocation derived in a principled way from the theory, and the experiments across ImageNet, maze navigation, and math reasoning sufficient.
QgFykzzb4A.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate scale equalization from simply allocating more rollouts to difficult prompts.

f2fVkuN9lT.one_liner: Diffusion transformer conditioned on a coarse mesh and multi-view sketches generates volumetric fields traced into 3D hair strands.
f2fVkuN9lT.problem: Existing hair modeling needs costly per-instance optimization to fit hair priors to foundation-model meshes and 2D orientations from predictors trained on limited hair data, restricting efficiency and generalization.
f2fVkuN9lT.method: HairFlow conditions strand generation on a coarse mesh for global shape and multi-view sketches for local strand flow, using an Orientation VAE and a conditioned diffusion transformer to generate volumetric fields that are traced into explicit strands. An automatic pipeline synthesizes geometrically aligned multi-view sketches in diverse styles to supply the missing paired training data.
f2fVkuN9lT.key_idea: Condition a diffusion transformer on a coarse mesh and multi-view sketches to generate a volumetric field that is traced into strands, replacing per-instance optimization.
f2fVkuN9lT.evidence: Experiments across diverse hairstyles with comparisons to prior work such as HairLRM and HairGPT (per reviews); the abstract names no datasets.
f2fVkuN9lT.claimed_gains: not stated numerically (the abstract claims plausible strands that follow the input conditions and substantially reduced inference time); a reviewer cites an 87x speedup over HairLRM's latent optimization, though the full single-image pipeline still takes 4-5 minutes.
f2fVkuN9lT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reconstruction quality is visually strong across complex hairstyles, and that combining a coarse mesh with multi-view sketches gives complementary global and local control.
f2fVkuN9lT.main_concern: Validation is limited for occluded and back views and for sensitivity to upstream multi-view generation quality, and ablations on camera and number of views are missing.

lbdjOpFBze.one_liner: Shows LLM judges' verdicts come from fixed-direction acceptance and rejection attention heads and calibrates their voting strengths.
lbdjOpFBze.problem: It is unclear how LLM judges, which encode correctness-related information internally, convert it into a final verdict.
lbdjOpFBze.method: The verdict-logit margin is decomposed into per-attention-head contributions to find static-voting head groups, whose causal effect is confirmed by ablation. Voting Calibration then uses an internal correctness signal from a small reference set to modulate voting strengths while preserving each head's direction.
lbdjOpFBze.key_idea: Attention heads vote in fixed directions (accept or reject) with input-dependent strengths; Voting Calibration rescales those strengths using an internal correctness signal instead of suppressing either camp.
lbdjOpFBze.evidence: Head-level decomposition and ablations across four models and several verdict formats, with Voting Calibration evaluated on the mu-MATH benchmark.
lbdjOpFBze.claimed_gains: Voting Calibration improves overall accuracy by 8.3% and true-negative rate by 14.6% on average across four models on the mu-MATH benchmark.
lbdjOpFBze.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the head-level static-voting finding intuitive and consistent across four models, with ablations giving causal evidence.
lbdjOpFBze.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the improvement comes from the supervised correctness probe rather than the voting mechanism, and baseline and intervention are not evaluated on identical test subsets.

54FPrnjjFZ.one_liner: Pre-trains encoder-decoder context compressors (LCLMs) that map long prompts to shorter latent sequences consumed by a decoder.
54FPrnjjFZ.problem: KV-cache compression either degrades quality or needs heavy compute per prompt, and existing encoder-decoder compressors are not competitive with it on the accuracy-efficiency frontier.
54FPrnjjFZ.method: The authors search over encoder-decoder architectures by pre-training many variants from scratch, then continually pre-train a family of 0.6B-encoder, 4B-decoder models on nearly 400B tokens each at compression ratios of 1:4, 1:8, and 1:16.
54FPrnjjFZ.key_idea: Compress long inputs with an encoder into a shorter latent sequence before decoder prefill, so the decoder never materializes the full KV cache.
54FPrnjjFZ.evidence: A controlled architecture search, then comparisons with KV-cache compression baselines (such as SnapKV and KVzip) on LongBench and RULER with time-to-first-token and peak-memory measurements on a single H200 (per reviews).
54FPrnjjFZ.claimed_gains: LCLMs improve the Pareto frontier across general-task performance, compression speed, and peak memory; a reviewer cites 46.04 on LongBench EN16 at 4x compression versus 45.21 for the original decoder.
54FPrnjjFZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a controlled architecture search under matched conditions and strong accuracy, time-to-first-token, and memory results from compressing before decoder prefill.
54FPrnjjFZ.main_concern: The efficiency comparison relies on unoptimized Hugging Face and kvpress implementations, and reported numbers differ between the main and ablation tables.

tdB5N7Z1m1.one_liner: MLLM that parses planar geometry diagrams into primitives and question-relevant theorems using a theorem-oriented formal language and RL.
tdB5N7Z1m1.problem: Current MLLMs entangle theorem identification and deduction in lengthy reasoning, struggle to identify relevant theorems, and leave deduction prone to unsupported assumptions.
tdB5N7Z1m1.method: Thoth is fine-tuned on GT-210K, a synthetic dataset annotated in the Theorem-oriented Formal Language (TOFL), then trained with reinforcement learning using fine-grained process rewards that ground theorem predictions in visual evidence and problem constraints.
tdB5N7Z1m1.key_idea: Represent diagrams as primitives plus theorem instances in a formal language, and reward theorem predictions through process signals tied to supporting visual evidence.
tdB5N7Z1m1.evidence: Theorem grounding on 600 synthetic diagrams and theorem-name selection on 200 real samples, plus downstream accuracy on four geometry VQA benchmarks and component ablations (per reviews).
tdB5N7Z1m1.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims strong theorem grounding, better primitive prediction, and improved downstream reasoning on four geometry VQA benchmarks, without figures).
tdB5N7Z1m1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the split into what to see, what knowledge applies, and how to deduce valuable, with TOFL giving an interpretable intermediate representation and validation spanning parsing, theorem identification, and downstream solving.
tdB5N7Z1m1.main_concern: Direct evidence of theorem binding on real diagrams is limited, with mostly synthetic evaluation and small downstream gains for strong models (about 1% per one reviewer).

Trv3yzv3M2.one_liner: Pre-training diagnostic scoring node-classification datasets by feature, topology, and label signal with a fixed logistic-regression probe.
Trv3yzv3M2.problem: Node classification benchmarks favor very different model interfaces, yet datasets are commonly summarized by homophily alone.
Trv3yzv3M2.method: Node Signal Atlas computes a Feature Signal Score, a Topology Signal Score, and a Label Signal Score, each from the same fixed logistic-regression probe on inexpensive annulus-based descriptors, without training a GNN.
Trv3yzv3M2.key_idea: Fit one fixed logistic-regression probe on annulus-based feature, topology, and label-context descriptors to measure where predictive signal is accessible.
Trv3yzv3M2.evidence: A controlled 24-dataset synthetic suite, 20 real benchmarks, and a frozen cross-generator architecture-selection benchmark.
Trv3yzv3M2.claimed_gains: not stated as figures (the abstract says NSA improves over scalar node homophily for architecture selection, a richer homophily profile is a stronger standalone baseline, and combining the two gives the best low-budget triage).
Trv3yzv3M2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find characterizing where predictive signal is accessible, beyond homophily, a meaningful idea, with useful controlled synthetic experiments and an explicit scope boundary.
Trv3yzv3M2.main_concern: The three signal scores are not cleanly disentangled, since the feature score uses multi-hop neighborhood statistics, which weakens their interpretation per model family.

kaov8fd1BB.one_liner: Benchmark testing whether deep-research agents can retrieve forecasting-relevant context from a document corpus, ignore distractors, and improve forecasts.
kaov8fd1BB.problem: Context-aided forecasting benchmarks assume the supporting context is already provided, leaving open whether agents can discover it from noisy, heterogeneous sources.
kaov8fd1BB.method: Dr-CiK asks agents to retrieve supporting context from a document corpus, filter distractors, distill evidence, and generate forecasts, with labeled supporting evidence and several distractor types so each step is evaluated separately.
kaov8fd1BB.key_idea: Pair a corpus of evidence-chain-derived documents and distractors with forecasting targets, so retrieval, distractor avoidance, and forecast gain are scored separately.
kaov8fd1BB.evidence: Context ablations and evaluations of deep research and forecasting methods paired together, including CODEX with GPT-5.5 and methods based on Gemini-3 Flash (per reviews).
kaov8fd1BB.claimed_gains: not stated (findings: high-quality context substantially improves forecasting, while existing deep research methods recover limited ground-truth evidence, are often misled by distractors, and can make forecasts worse than with no context).
kaov8fd1BB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that whether agents can find the right context is an important, novel question, with a solid human-verified data pipeline and annotations that support failure diagnosis.
kaov8fd1BB.main_concern: The benchmark relies on a largely synthetic corpus and a predefined reference evidence chain, so it may measure retrieval and filtering rather than deep research and penalize valid alternative evidence paths.

jdST9ehQcf.one_liner: Amortized batch Bayesian optimization that samples batches in one pass from a flow-matching model trained on refined Thompson-sampling argmaxes.
jdST9ehQcf.problem: Conventional batch Bayesian optimization needs increasingly hard batch-selection procedures as batch size grows, while a batch must cover several promising regions without redundant evaluations in few rounds.
jdST9ehQcf.method: FMTR learns offline, by conditional flow matching on Thompson-sampling argmaxes refined toward high-value regions via a horizon-dependent Langevin pushforward map, a history-conditioned proposal distribution from which variable-size batches are sampled. At test time the parameters stay fixed, with no surrogate refitting or numerical acquisition optimization.
jdST9ehQcf.key_idea: Train a history-conditioned flow-matching sampler offline on Langevin-refined Thompson-sampling argmaxes, so a batch of any size is generated in one forward pass.
jdST9ehQcf.evidence: Synthetic and real-world benchmarks against batch BO and in-context baselines, with ablations on the trend term, Langevin refinement, and tilted target (per reviews).
jdST9ehQcf.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims strong performance against batch BO and in-context baselines and substantially lower batch-selection cost, without figures).
jdST9ehQcf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find amortizing batch construction into a learned sampler sensible, with substantial ablations, no test-time surrogate refitting, and good empirical results.
jdST9ehQcf.main_concern: Novelty and baselines are thin: the method mainly reproduces refined Thompson-sampling proposals with flow matching, and key related methods such as NAP are not compared experimentally.

2bJYHmEQst.one_liner: Quasi-Newton optimizers for deep learning with built-in positive-definite curvature and Newton-Schulz matrix operations in diagonal and Kronecker-factored forms.
2bJYHmEQst.problem: Non-convexity and enormous parameter counts have limited the use of quasi-Newton methods in deep learning.
2bJYHmEQst.method: SoftServe derives positive-definite curvature estimates from the variational objective of Berglund et al. (2025), even with negative curvature, in diagonal and Kronecker-factored variants that stay positive definite by construction. It uses the coupled Newton-Schulz iteration instead of matrix decompositions, with no line searches or ad hoc curvature corrections.
2bJYHmEQst.key_idea: Obtain positive-definite curvature from a variational secant objective that stays well defined under negative curvature, and compute the required matrix operations with GPU-friendly Newton-Schulz iterations.
2bJYHmEQst.evidence: Ill-conditioned problems including recurrent networks, deep autoencoders, physics-informed neural networks, and a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model, against Adam, Muon, and SOAP, with Newton-Schulz accuracy and penalty ablations (per reviews).
2bJYHmEQst.claimed_gains: Often achieves lower losses than Adam, Muon, and SOAP on severely ill-conditioned problems, including a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model; no other figures are stated.
2bJYHmEQst.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear mathematical construction that keeps curvature positive definite under negative curvature, with detailed implementation and evaluation against strong optimizer baselines.
2bJYHmEQst.main_concern: The positive-definiteness guarantee covers exact updates, not the finite-iteration FP32 Newton-Schulz implementation, and robustness studies are limited to small benchmarks.
