w4aVbnUOpC.one_liner: Benchmark of 398 theorem-level proof-discovery tasks from STOC and COLT 2026 papers, built with a reusable pipeline.
w4aVbnUOpC.problem: Research-level reasoning in LLMs is hard to evaluate systematically beyond competition mathematics.
w4aVbnUOpC.method: TCSAlgBench converts theorem statements from 138 STOC and COLT 2026 papers into self-contained challenges: expert-designed rules complete paper-specific context, preserve computational assumptions and quantitative guarantees, and withhold constructions when discovering an algorithm is part of the task. Provers receive theorem statements and access to cited prior work.
w4aVbnUOpC.key_idea: Rewrite theorems from newly released papers into self-contained proof-discovery tasks using expert-designed repair rules, so the benchmark can be refreshed with versioned batches.
w4aVbnUOpC.evidence: Ten model configurations from four families under direct inference and prover-verifier discussion, plus four agent workflows under matched model-call opportunities, all on the full benchmark.
w4aVbnUOpC.claimed_gains: GPT-5.6 Sol max reaches the highest five-run verifier-accepted coverage at 23.6% after 10-round discussion, and discussion and repeated sampling improve coverage.
w4aVbnUOpC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a valuable evaluation gap with research-level theoretical CS tasks, and credit the reusable pipeline for a refreshable benchmark and the broad model and agent evaluation.
w4aVbnUOpC.main_concern: Only 61 of 398 challenges were human-reviewed, so construction errors and answer leakage are not quantified, and the low pass rate is hard to interpret without a validity ceiling.

YjZnFXxw4o.one_liner: Wraps static agent environments in plug-in components synthesized from diagnosed policy flaws, keeping each environment's original verifier.
YjZnFXxw4o.problem: Hand-built agent training environments are static, blind to an agent's weaknesses and quickly outgrown, and existing generation methods need domain-specific pipelines and expensive or unreliable verifiers.
YjZnFXxw4o.method: EnvHarness is a programmable layer of plug-in components that reshapes a static environment's behavior without modifying its underlying logic. EnvRigger treats the policy as a black box, observes execution trajectories, synthesizes components targeting diagnosed flaws, and validates them with fresh rollouts.
YjZnFXxw4o.key_idea: Wrap an existing environment with synthesized plug-in components that target flaws diagnosed from policy trajectories, validated by fresh rollouts, so the original verifier still applies.
YjZnFXxw4o.evidence: Five benchmarks in four domains under skill learning and reinforcement learning, compared with original environments and domain-specific environment generation pipelines such as GenEnv (per reviews).
YjZnFXxw4o.claimed_gains: Up to a 9.0-point improvement on held-out instances with 9.8% fewer execution steps.
YjZnFXxw4o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reusing existing environments and verifiers while reshaping their conditions a well-motivated approach to environment scaling, with comprehensive evaluation across five benchmarks.
YjZnFXxw4o.main_concern: The contribution is not disentangled from simpler interventions such as fixed wrappers or skills from the same diagnoses, the method is engineering-heavy, and the reinforcement-learning results are mixed.

mFZHXvTZJu.one_liner: Generative latent-geometry model that infers entity embeddings on product manifolds from grouped count data via Riemannian Langevin sampling.
mFZHXvTZJu.problem: When no observed graph exists and relatedness must be inferred from grouped counts across heterogeneous contexts, it is unclear when pooling information through a shared geometry beats estimating each pair alone.
mFZHXvTZJu.method: Entity positions on a product manifold determine a pairwise propensity linked to overdispersed counts by an observation layer, and the posterior is sampled with Riemannian stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics. A derived variance ratio between the geometric estimate and a pair-only fit yields a combined estimator with no extra fitted parameters.
mFZHXvTZJu.key_idea: Place entities on a product manifold to define pairwise propensity, and derive a variance ratio showing pooled geometric estimates beat pair-only fits when endpoints are well determined.
mFZHXvTZJu.evidence: Cancer co-mutation, protein-interaction, mitochondrial-variant, and movie co-rating data, with flat versus hyperbolic geometry comparisons and synthetic data per reviews.
mFZHXvTZJu.claimed_gains: On cancer co-mutation data, 5% of an entity's evidence suffices to outpredict full-evidence baselines on two thirds of genes; on mitochondrial variants, hyperbolic geometry outperforms flat models under the same likelihood.
mFZHXvTZJu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find inferring relatedness from grouped counts a practical problem and the variance analysis a useful way to understand when shared embeddings help, with encouraging biological experiments.
mFZHXvTZJu.main_concern: The variance-ratio theory rests on approximations (other embeddings held fixed, isotropic neighborhoods) whose error is not quantified, and baselines are limited to classical pairwise estimators and older embedding methods.

VwZ2RCKhVp.one_liner: Controlled comparison of in-context versus layer-wise visual injection in VLMs, analyzing how visual tokens evolve inside the LLM.
VwZ2RCKhVp.problem: How the choice of vision integration architecture affects visual information and its internal transformation inside the LLM is underexplored under controlled conditions.
VwZ2RCKhVp.method: The study trains in-context and layer-wise injection VLMs under identical conditions and evaluates them on single-image, multi-image, and video benchmarks, then analyzes visual-token representations and frequency-based interventions to explain the performance gap.
VwZ2RCKhVp.key_idea: Hold encoder, connector, backbone, data, and hyperparameters fixed while varying only how visual tokens enter the LLM, then trace token representations and frequency content layer by layer.
VwZ2RCKhVp.evidence: Two backbone families and several scales across about 20 benchmarks in single-image, multi-image, and video understanding, with representation analysis and low-pass frequency interventions (per reviews).
VwZ2RCKhVp.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says in-context injection consistently outperforms layer-wise injection, with the largest gaps on OCR, without figures).
VwZ2RCKhVp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the well-controlled comparison across backbones, scales, and benchmarks, plus complementary representation and frequency analyses.
VwZ2RCKhVp.main_concern: Findings overlap prior controlled comparisons such as NVLM, and the frequency-intervention evidence does not establish that frequency sensitivity explains the performance gap.

MLE0ZSHwTs.one_liner: Offline-to-online RL with one-step flow policies trained via adjoint critic-gradient propagation and noise-conditioned distributional Q-chunking.
MLE0ZSHwTs.problem: Straight-flow policies cut inference cost but struggle to use critic guidance along flow trajectories and to capture distributional returns while reducing bootstrapping bias.
MLE0ZSHwTs.method: Q-Adjoint Anchoring applies Adjoint Matching to propagate critic gradients along straight flow trajectories without multi-step forward SDE integration. Noise-conditioned Q-Chunking estimates optimistic values within the return distribution while limiting bias accumulation and keeping a short policy execution horizon.
MLE0ZSHwTs.key_idea: Propagate critic gradients along straight flows with Adjoint Matching, and learn noise-conditioned chunked value estimates that give optimistic values from the return distribution.
MLE0ZSHwTs.evidence: Robotic locomotion and manipulation tasks against baselines such as QAM, DQC, and CGQ, with ablations of action chunking, adjoint matching, and distributional returns (per reviews).
MLE0ZSHwTs.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims high computational efficiency and strong task performance, with its headline success figure cut off).
MLE0ZSHwTs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the design addresses complementary problems, expressive one-step policies and long-horizon value learning, with theoretical justification and systematic component analysis.
MLE0ZSHwTs.main_concern: Reproduced baseline scores are substantially lower than those in prior work, and ablations and horizon comparisons are limited, making the relative gains hard to assess.

CDnkuVs7ki.one_liner: Sparse autoencoder that learns mixed-topology feature graphs by competing complete parent sets, using the graph as a training loss.
CDnkuVs7ki.problem: Structured SAEs impose single-parent trees or forests, while post-hoc graphs allow multiple parents but neither guide feature learning nor ensure reliable relation recovery.
CDnkuVs7ki.method: AG-SAE treats each feature's complete parent set as one structural hypothesis and competes it against null, subset, and alternative explanations so evidence selects zero, one, or multiple parents. The induced topology defines a differentiable structural loss and guides refinement (absorption mitigation, new features from reconstruction gaps), and the graph is re-induced from the revised dictionary.
CDnkuVs7ki.key_idea: Select each feature's complete parent set by competing it against null, subset, and alternative hypotheses, then feed the graph back as a structural loss in a dictionary-graph cycle.
CDnkuVs7ki.evidence: Exact mixed-topology recovery in a controlled toy model, and experiments on LLM activations (mainly Gemma-2-2B per reviews) covering relational reliability, semantic validity, causal interventions, and ablations against structured and post-hoc baselines.
CDnkuVs7ki.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims exact mixed-topology recovery in a toy model and greater relational reliability and semantic validity than baselines, without figures).
CDnkuVs7ki.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find complete parent-set induction and iterative dictionary-graph refinement an interesting step beyond single-parent SAEs, validated in both toy and real LLM settings.
CDnkuVs7ki.main_concern: Experiments are mostly on a small model (Gemma-2-2B) with parent sets of at most three and no scaling analysis, and the contributions of individual components are unclear.

RhBMJ6DiHi.one_liner: Bayesian graph model assigning each edge a symmetric positive-definite matrix, with posterior inference on how edge matrices change across contexts.
RhBMJ6DiHi.problem: A single scalar edge weight cannot describe direction-dependent interactions between nodes that carry feature vectors.
RhBMJ6DiHi.method: BMWG infers a posterior over SPD edge matrices in each context, measures change between contexts with the affine-invariant Riemannian geodesic distance, shows strengthening and weakening directions via generalized eigenvalues, and separates real change from finite-sample variation with a same-truth reference.
RhBMJ6DiHi.key_idea: Replace scalar edge weights with identifiable SPD matrices and compare contexts by AIRM geodesic distance and generalized eigenvalues against a same-truth reference.
RhBMJ6DiHi.evidence: Proofs of identifiability, strict log-concavity, and asymptotic normality of the posterior; controlled experiments against fused graphical lasso, Bayesian multiple-GGM, and common principal components; Bay Area weather data from Meteostat; and a TCGA analysis (per reviews).
RhBMJ6DiHi.claimed_gains: not stated as figures (the abstract says BMWG recovers the precision matrix competitively with fused graphical lasso and multiple-GGM and recovers edge-change directions more accurately than common principal components; on weather data, a 12-hour state change alters spatial coupling about as much as the seasonal difference).
RhBMJ6DiHi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the matrix-valued edge formulation a clear, interpretable extension of scalar edge weights that captures the direction of change, with identifiability results.
RhBMJ6DiHi.main_concern: The contribution is mainly an integration of established techniques with unclear novelty over multivariate graphical models, synthetic tests are generated from the model itself, and real-data evaluations are small.

8NsJkTwWtd.one_liner: Measures consistency and specificity of language model circuits at component and neuron level across six tasks and five models.
8NsJkTwWtd.problem: Circuits are typically evaluated by necessity and sufficiency, which say little about whether a circuit consistently captures how the model performs a task or is specific to that task.
8NsJkTwWtd.method: The authors extract circuits at the component level (attention heads, MLP blocks) and the individual MLP-neuron level, then measure within-task consistency, cross-task specificity, and circuit overlap, with a case study of attention heads shared across task circuits.
8NsJkTwWtd.key_idea: Quantify circuits by consistency across inputs of the same task and by specificity, comparing accuracy drops from ablating a task's own circuit versus another task's circuit.
8NsJkTwWtd.evidence: Six tasks and five models, with circuits from EAP-IG and RelP attribution at component and neuron levels, plus a case study of shared attention heads.
8NsJkTwWtd.claimed_gains: not stated (empirical findings: component-level circuits are consistent but not specific, since ablating a task's own circuit drops accuracy about as much as ablating another task's, while neuron-level circuits are more specific but far less consistent).
8NsJkTwWtd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find it a valid and novel question, with extensive, systematic experiments across tasks, models, attribution methods, and granularities.
8NsJkTwWtd.main_concern: The causes of the observed lack of specificity are not tested, and the consistency requirement may conflict with input-dependent mechanisms reported in the literature.

poF40nTMYK.one_liner: Agent that actively queries longitudinal EHR records and imaging tools to acquire evidence, instead of reading pre-curated inputs.
poF40nTMYK.problem: Clinical LLM systems assume evidence has already been curated and handed to the model, whereas real workflows require seeking and synthesizing multimodal evidence from heterogeneous sources.
poF40nTMYK.method: Given a clinical task and raw patient data, ClinSeekAgent queries longitudinal EHR records, invokes imaging analysis tools, refines hypotheses as evidence arrives, and integrates it into grounded decisions. It is validated as an inference-time agent for frontier LLMs and as a training pipeline for open-source models.
poF40nTMYK.key_idea: Replace passive evidence consumption with iterative, tool-based evidence acquisition over raw EHR and imaging data, refining hypotheses as new information appears.
poF40nTMYK.evidence: ClinSeek-Bench with 13 text-only EHR task categories and 6 multimodal EHR-chest X-ray categories, pairing each question with Curated Input and raw patient data, plus full-record and single-pass-retrieval ablations (per reviews).
poF40nTMYK.claimed_gains: Without benchmark-specific curation, ClinSeekAgent significantly outperforms curated input for both Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol; the abstract excerpt is cut off before figures.
poF40nTMYK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find moving from curated to actively sought evidence well motivated, with a useful paired benchmark and extensive experiments whose ablations show the benefit of iterative seeking.
poF40nTMYK.main_concern: Gains are not separated from additional test-time computation (several model calls per question versus one for Curated Input), and the framework looks like a standard tool-using agent without comparison to existing EHR agents.

OqTORthRVE.one_liner: Accelerates few-step interactive world models by selecting anchor frames by interaction sensitivity and reconstructing skipped features with phase-aware residuals.
OqTORthRVE.problem: Existing acceleration methods for interactive world models can miss heterogeneous control responses and spatial transport when recovering skipped features.
OqTORthRVE.method: CAST is a reconstruction-coupled inference framework that selects anchors by interaction sensitivity and cross-layer coverage, reconstructs skipped residuals with frequency- and confidence-aware Phase-Aware Reconstruction (PAR), and routes historical KV according to downstream reconstruction responsibility.
OqTORthRVE.key_idea: Couple anchor selection, phase-based residual reconstruction of skipped features, and historical KV routing so that anchor errors that propagate to skipped frames drive the sparse-attention budget.
OqTORthRVE.evidence: Experiments on Matrix-Game 3.0 and HY-World 1.5, scored with VBench and thirteen WorldMark dimensions against compared acceleration baselines.
OqTORthRVE.claimed_gains: 2.15× and 3.48× speedups on Matrix-Game 3.0 and HY-World 1.5 with the highest VBench scores among compared methods, and leads non-native baselines on seven and six of thirteen WorldMark dimensions.
OqTORthRVE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the three components (anchor selection, phase-aware reconstruction, coupled KV routing) coherent and the speed-quality trade-off favorable on two backbones.
OqTORthRVE.main_concern: The claim of the best quality-efficiency balance rests on single operating points (some slower baselines are more faithful), and reviewers ask for harder-motion evaluation and end-to-end latency measurements.

inX0diLejS.one_liner: Paired-intervention benchmark with size-matched nulls showing that action-change scores do not measure chain-of-thought faithfulness in VLAs.
inX0diLejS.problem: The standard test of CoT faithfulness in vision-language-action models scores a reasoning edit by how often it moves the action, which may not reflect reliance on the reasoning.
inX0diLejS.method: CoT-Faith is a paired-intervention benchmark with 13 edit families, size-matched nulls and closed-loop evaluation, applied to 11 token-decoded VLA configurations from two model lineages. It also uses a direction-aware score that requires the action to point the implied direction.
inX0diLejS.key_idea: Score reasoning edits against size- and tag-matched null edits and require the action to move in the direction the edit implies, not merely to change.
inX0diLejS.evidence: 11 VLA configurations from two lineages under teacher-forced scoring, plus closed-loop LIBERO evaluation of two competent policies with edited or emptied reasoning.
inX0diLejS.claimed_gains: Two judge-validated floors give opposite verdicts on 10 of 11 configurations, direction flips beat their null on 11 of 11, and the direction-aware score moves the top-ranked model from first of eight to seventh.
inX0diLejS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the question as important, the benchmark as thorough, and the finding that two meaning-preserving controls give opposite verdicts as informative.
inX0diLejS.main_concern: The meaning-preserving controls are validated by a single LLM judge that flips 17.6% of judgments when presentation order is reversed, on about 40 pairs per family, and a grounded model may legitimately ignore an edited CoT.

NAq74qp8IJ.one_liner: Agent-curated 100K benchmark for AI-edited image manipulation localization, plus a phase-aware semantic-forensic localization network.
NAq74qp8IJ.problem: Existing image manipulation detection and localization benchmarks lack visual realism, manipulation diversity, and generator coverage for recent generative image editing.
NAq74qp8IJ.method: Disguise-Agent, a closed-loop agent (scene perception, editing planning, execution, quality validation, iterative reflection), generates 100K manipulated images with pixel-level masks from seven AIGC models across three manipulation types. PhaseAware-Net (PANet) adds local phase modeling and Forensic-Semantic Consistency (FSC) learning.
NAq74qp8IJ.key_idea: Generate edited images and masks with a closed-loop agent that validates and reflects, and localize edits by enforcing consistency between semantic and phase-based forensic features.
NAq74qp8IJ.evidence: The abstract is cut off before its results; reviewers cite PANet comparisons with Mesorch and M2SFormer on Impostor and cross-domain tests on CocoGlide, AutoSplice and BR-Gen.
NAq74qp8IJ.claimed_gains: not stated; the TL;DR and abstract claim strong cross-domain generalization in localization and detection without numbers.
NAq74qp8IJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see Impostor as a valuable multi-generator, multi-region benchmark with multi-stage quality checks that is harder than existing recent AIGC sets.
NAq74qp8IJ.main_concern: Generalization claims outrun the evidence (every generator appears in both train and test, with no leave-one-generator-out result), mask accuracy is not quantified, and PANet is seen as incremental next to the dataset.

vRVjeJJF6T.one_liner: Neural rigid-body simulator that reasons over sparse neighborhoods of contact surface points and propagates contact effects within each body.
vRVjeJJF6T.problem: End-to-end world models predict whole scenes or objects, yet rigid-body contact is local, so capturing how local surface contacts shape object motion remains challenging.
vRVjeJJF6T.method: RiCo represents interactions through sparse neighborhoods of contact surface points, combining each point's state with the relative geometry, motion and physical properties of nearby surfaces. It then reasons across the object's points to determine how the contacts jointly affect its motion.
vRVjeJJF6T.key_idea: Confine cross-object reasoning to nearby surface points and propagate contact information within each rigid body, avoiding all-pairs interactions between scene points.
vRVjeJJF6T.evidence: Experiments on the MOVi benchmark (MOVi-A and MOVi-B per reviewers) against mesh-based and point-based baselines, measuring 100-frame position and orientation errors and penetration.
vRVjeJJF6T.claimed_gains: Reduces 100-frame position errors by 31–35% and orientation errors by approximately 38% versus baselines on MOVi, with higher contact fidelity.
vRVjeJJF6T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the local contact representation well motivated and the position, orientation and penetration results strong on MOVi.
vRVjeJJF6T.main_concern: The ablations do not separate explicit cross-object contact encoding from other coupled differences with the closest point-based baseline, and reviewers also question novelty and the rigid-only scope.

si7vKoj70j.one_liner: Couples a navigation VLM, trained with rejection sampling and AI-feedback RL, to a world-action manipulation model for dexterous mobile manipulation.
si7vKoj70j.problem: Navigation is too coarse for manipulation, which needs a precise base position and approach orientation, and navigation and manipulation are trained in isolation without a feedback loop.
si7vKoj70j.method: Nav4Manip-N is trained in three stages: multi-task co-tuning with manipulation-aware affordance prediction, rejection sampling fine-tuning (RFT) on retained policy-generated paths, and RLAIF with counterfactual preferences. Nav4Manip-M trains a world-action model (WAM) for downstream dexterous manipulation.
si7vKoj70j.key_idea: Refine the navigation policy with manipulation feedback (affordance prediction, rejection-sampled trajectories, counterfactual AI preferences) so the stopping pose is manipulation-ready.
si7vKoj70j.evidence: The abstract is cut off before its results; reviewers cite the Nav4Manip-Pairs dataset, multiple benchmarks, simulator-based fine-tuning, and a stage ablation table.
si7vKoj70j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gap between navigation success and manipulation-ready stopping is an important problem and that the dataset and system form a coherent contribution.
si7vKoj70j.main_concern: The co-evolution claim is weak because the manipulation WAM stays frozen after post-training, and RFT adds only a marginal gain (31.01% to 31.79% end-to-end success).

ij0HAgXUbp.one_liner: Three-stage world-action model pretrained action-free on Internet egocentric videos, then aligned to actions in simulation, for language-conditioned local navigation.
ij0HAgXUbp.problem: End-to-end navigation policies need diverse training data, but real-robot data is costly to collect and simulated data leaves a sim-to-real gap.
ij0HAgXUbp.method: ScaleNav first runs instruction-conditioned video pretraining on Internet egocentric videos, then aligns actions with action-labeled simulated data to predict executable action chunks, and finally fine-tunes all trainable components jointly for navigation.
ij0HAgXUbp.key_idea: Learn goal-directed visual dynamics from action-free Internet egocentric video and reuse them to support action-chunk generation in a unified world-action model.
ij0HAgXUbp.evidence: Evaluated on a single-view adaptation of Short-Horizon OVON and the HabitatGS-LN benchmark, against baselines including StreamVLN and Uni-NaVid, plus deployment on a real quadruped robot.
ij0HAgXUbp.claimed_gains: 86.5% success on a single-view adaptation of Short-Horizon OVON and 94.9% on HabitatGS-LN, outperforming the evaluated baselines.
ij0HAgXUbp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the interpretable evaluation design and the strong real-robot results with fast inference.
ij0HAgXUbp.main_concern: The ablation does not isolate the benefit of Internet videos (the full model gets extra Stage 1 updates and a changed video source), and recent baselines such as NaVILA or OmniNav are missing.

z5Wm4zp04O.one_liner: Bayesian filter that stores the posterior in flow-matching model weights and updates them by gradient descent at test time.
z5Wm4zp04O.problem: Generative filters either propagate a finite sample ensemble or repeatedly sample trajectories, coupling online cost to ensemble size or sampling budget in high-dimensional systems.
z5Wm4zp04O.method: The Belief Flow Filter (BFF) carries the belief in flow-matching model weights, updates them by gradient descent at test time with a Bayes-derived loss, and samples the posterior from the updated model without a Gaussian restriction.
z5Wm4zp04O.key_idea: Encode the evolving posterior in flow-matching network weights and update them with a Bayes-derived test-time loss, so each observation costs a gradient step instead of ensemble propagation.
z5Wm4zp04O.evidence: Five physical systems (1D-PDE, 2D-PDE, low-dimensional ODE and a tokamak simulation per reviewers), plus an idealized expressivity result and a population-level bound linking training loss to filtering error.
z5Wm4zp04O.claimed_gains: Lowest reconstruction error and continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) across five physical systems; the abstract is cut off before further numbers.
z5Wm4zp04O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find carrying the belief in generator weights an interesting alternative to particle filtering, with competitive results on chaotic and multimodal systems.
z5Wm4zp04O.main_concern: The weight-space advantage is not isolated (the update is rank-one per probe and the GRU control is not matched), a single conditional flow-model baseline is missing, and cost comparisons are incomplete.

MkGCt28yKg.one_liner: Exploratory Nash Policy Optimization pairs SFT regularization with an adversarial explorer to remove exponential KL-parameter dependence in iterative Nash learning.
MkGCt28yKg.problem: Standard iterative NLHF can suffer an exponential dependence on the KL-regularization parameter because implicit exploration through policy updates is insufficient, and existing regret guarantees need a general preference model and minimax oracles.
MkGCt28yKg.method: ENPO combines SFT-based regularization with adversarial policy exploration and needs no minimax oracle or explicit preference model estimation. BENPO adds an explicit exploration bonus with extra oracles for an O(log T) regret bound, and Direct ENPO is the practical variant.
MkGCt28yKg.key_idea: Add an adversarial sampler that targets weaknesses of the current policy, together with SFT regularization, so exploration is explicit rather than implicit in policy updates.
MkGCt28yKg.evidence: Theory (an explicit lower bound for iterative NLHF and regret bounds for ENPO and BENPO) plus experiments on Llama-3-8B-Instruct compared with INPO and XPO per reviewers.
MkGCt28yKg.claimed_gains: ENPO eliminates the exponential dependency without minimax oracles or explicit preference models, and BENPO guarantees an O(log T) regret bound.
MkGCt28yKg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider exploration under general preferences important and the theoretical results (the INPO lower bound and BENPO's logarithmic bound) meaningful.
MkGCt28yKg.main_concern: Experiments are narrow (one Llama-3-8B-Instruct backbone, only INPO and XPO as baselines), and the theory hides a steep preference-query cost and relies on strong assumptions.

V7wmvX2QcU.one_liner: Predicts a characteristic learning rate from a statistical-physics balance of stochastic exploration and curvature confinement, estimated from a few mini-batches.
V7wmvX2QcU.problem: Learning-rate selection for adaptive optimizers remains empirical and costly, usually done by comparing final performance across multiple training runs.
V7wmvX2QcU.method: The paper derives a statistical-physics prediction of an optimal characteristic learning rate alpha_c from the competition between stochastic exploration and curvature-induced confinement under second-moment-shaped mobility. It estimates alpha_c from a few mini-batches at a cost of 31 gradient-equivalent steps.
V7wmvX2QcU.key_idea: Define alpha_c as the learning rate where second-moment-shaped stochastic mobility balances curvature-induced confinement, measured from mini-batch gradient statistics rather than final performance.
V7wmvX2QcU.evidence: Experiments on deep neural networks and large language models, compared with seven inexpensive selection baselines, plus a measurable criterion for the predictor's applicability regime.
V7wmvX2QcU.claimed_gains: Estimates alpha_c at 31 gradient-equivalent steps, with the prediction near the generalization optimum and the best grid-search rate, and the highest development accuracy among seven inexpensive selection baselines.
V7wmvX2QcU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that choosing learning rates without dense tuning is practically important and that the low-cost predictor performs competitively with grid search.
V7wmvX2QcU.main_concern: The derivation depends on approximations (Gaussian mini-batch noise, self-consistent assumptions) that hold only at intermediate batch sizes, and transfer to larger transformers and LLMs is unclear.

5j5OsaQgCm.one_liner: Merges multimodal continual-learning experts using a minimal lossless input space for language weights plus a supervised visual calibrator.
5j5OsaQgCm.problem: A compact space can represent every expert update yet exclude their best shared reconstruction, so storing every update need not preserve the optimal merge.
5j5OsaQgCm.method: The paper establishes when an input restriction is lossless and identifies the unique minimal faithful space. FerVA then uses a static language solve that keeps full input features in compact output coordinates, and a supervised visual calibrator learned through an auxiliary decoder whose mixture is transferred to the constructed model.
5j5OsaQgCm.key_idea: Merge in output coordinates that retain full input features (the minimal faithful space) rather than restricting the input span, then calibrate a visual mixture through an auxiliary decoder.
5j5OsaQgCm.evidence: A controlled six-task UCIT study, a random-basis comparison at correction rank 16, and four UCIT/DCL-backbone settings against reproduced merged baselines.
5j5OsaQgCm.claimed_gains: Recovering the omitted component raises FAA from 69.54 to 76.04, and the full method reaches 76.20 on UCIT–LLaVA, 4.05 points above the strongest comparator; at correction rank 16, objective-guided recovery gives 75.54 versus 71.18–71.33 for three random bases.
5j5OsaQgCm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly motivated and theoretically grounded, with evaluation on two benchmarks and backbones that links the reconstruction argument to task performance.
5j5OsaQgCm.main_concern: The gain over the closest baseline (MAny) is not isolated from other construction and tuning choices, and ablations such as auxiliary-decoder versus direct calibration and multiple random seeds are missing.

FNzv0K8goS.one_liner: Merges multimodal experts by rebuilding rotary query-key attention operators under head-width limits, then calibrating a shared visual residual.
FNzv0K8goS.problem: Preserving query and key projections separately need not preserve their joint attention interaction, which in multimodal merging must also process visual features from a consolidated interface.
FNzv0K8goS.method: AttnCal reconstructs joint rotary-position operators under the original head-width constraint using expert weights alone, targeting the worst expert-relative reconstruction error within each head. It then calibrates the constructed Q/K factors under a fitted visual map, fixes the language weights, and adapts a shared visual residual.
FNzv0K8goS.key_idea: Construct merged Q/K factors that directly minimize worst-case per-head attention-logit reconstruction error, then calibrate them against a fitted visual map.
FNzv0K8goS.evidence: Four reproduced benchmark-backbone protocols, including six UCIT tasks with LLaVA-1.5-7B, plus computable objective bounds and a fixed-input attention-logit error guarantee.
FNzv0K8goS.claimed_gains: Highest FAA among merged baselines across four protocols; on six UCIT tasks with LLaVA-1.5-7B it reaches 76.07 FAA, 82.72 CAA and 0.33 BWT versus 72.15, 81.60 and -1.52 for the strongest FAA baseline.
FNzv0K8goS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the identification of the Q/K merging problem, the computable theoretical bounds, and consistent final-average gains across four benchmark-backbone settings.
FNzv0K8goS.main_concern: The gain is not tied to the Q/K construction (only the full pipeline is scored), and the Stage 2 visual calibration adds only about 0.40 FAA while a no-further-training setting scores higher in the handoff study.

1TWBSR1KPi.one_liner: One-step reference-based face restoration that routes only informative reference tokens through a pretrained multimodal diffusion transformer.
1TWBSR1KPi.problem: Reference images are input-dependently redundant, so dense processing wastes computation and may introduce mismatched textures or attributes into the restored face.
1TWBSR1KPi.method: RefRouteFR uses the native multimodal interface of a pretrained Diffusion Transformer for reference and text guidance. A lightweight router estimates each reference token's usefulness from the current multimodal context and forwards only the top subset through each block, while a learned latent calibrator reduces the mismatch between degraded latents and the pretrained flow prior.
1TWBSR1KPi.key_idea: A router scores reference tokens against the low-quality input and text context and sends only the highest-scoring subset through each transformer block, the rest bypassing computation.
1TWBSR1KPi.evidence: Experiments on multiple datasets (FFHQ-Ref per reviewers) with ablations on token budget, number of reference images, and router design.
1TWBSR1KPi.claimed_gains: Matches the quality of its dense counterpart while reducing inference time by approximately 40%, with restoration results claimed best on multiple datasets.
1TWBSR1KPi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the reference-token router as an effective, practical way to cut computation without an extra reference network, backed by thorough ablations.
1TWBSR1KPi.main_concern: Reviewers view the work as engineering adaptation of a pretrained DiT (the contribution of FLUX2 versus the method is untested), with unclear evaluation protocols, incomplete baselines, and possible prompt leakage.

0vAU1ZmGdI.one_liner: Adapts each expert before merging: distills its own-task predictions and matches the pretrained model on other tasks, using unlabeled data.
0vAU1ZmGdI.problem: Cross-task interference degrades merged experts because standard fine-tuning optimizes each expert on its own task without constraining how its update affects predictions on other tasks.
0vAU1ZmGdI.method: Resolving Interference (RI) independently adapts each expert before merging with unlabeled task data. It distills the original expert's predictions on its own task to preserve specialization and matches the shared pretrained model's predictions on other tasks.
0vAU1ZmGdI.key_idea: Dual distillation per expert keeps its own-task outputs while anchoring its outputs on other tasks' data to the pretrained model, limiting the task vector's off-task influence.
0vAU1ZmGdI.evidence: Vision and language benchmarks, combined with existing merging methods including test-time adaptation, plus consistency evaluations, qualitative generations, and Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B per reviewers.
0vAU1ZmGdI.claimed_gains: Surpasses the strongest evaluated baselines by up to 2.9% for language-model merging.
0vAU1ZmGdI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like addressing interference at the expert-adaptation stage with a simple objective that works with different merging operators and adds no inference-time overhead.
0vAU1ZmGdI.main_concern: There are no ablations of the two loss terms or sensitivity analysis of the fixed trade-off weight lambda, and the adaptation cost for large language models is not reported.

ThpZqtX7gS.one_liner: Schedules batched replacement of structured objects with compact retrieval Cards, trading waiting cost against cache-reconstruction cost, to preserve prefix-cache reuse.
ThpZqtX7gS.problem: In long-horizon agents the history is resent with every request and grows, and editing it can break prefix-cache reuse, while prior recoverable methods time edits by reuse forecasts or preset intervals.
ThpZqtX7gS.method: CADOC is an online algorithm that replaces structured objects with compact Cards while keeping their exact originals retrievable on demand. It commits replacements in batches by balancing accumulated waiting cost against shared cache-reconstruction cost, following an economic order quantity trade-off.
ThpZqtX7gS.key_idea: Commit Card replacements in batches when accumulated waiting cost exceeds the shared prefix-cache reconstruction cost, a rule derived from an economic-order-quantity trade-off.
ThpZqtX7gS.evidence: Fixed-history replays, online benchmark-chain evaluations (SWE and LongMemEval-V2 per reviewers) against full context and other configurations, and a hot-tail sweep, plus a result recovering the optimal integer batch under stationary assumptions.
ThpZqtX7gS.claimed_gains: Lowest aggregate input cost among the compared configurations, reducing input cost by approximately 70% on average while keeping task performance close to full context.
ThpZqtX7gS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the cache-aware cost framing a real systems issue, the reversible Card representation appealing, and the derived commit rule consistent with the replay results.
ThpZqtX7gS.main_concern: Cost savings rest on a weighted token-accounting model rather than measurements from a real serving endpoint, and the live results come from one chain per arm without error bars.

t3A04C8BRK.one_liner: Benchmark of 900 storybook transitions testing whether models generate a coherent next image, narration and speech, scored with consistency-centered judges.
t3A04C8BRK.problem: Omnimodal evaluation scores text, image and speech independently, although individually plausible outputs may not express a coherent shared event.
t3A04C8BRK.method: Each instance gives a current storybook page and structured next-page conditions, and the model must generate the next illustration, narration and spoken character utterance. Outputs are scored with modality-specific metrics and LLM-as-a-judge rubrics for context preservation, condition following, reference consistency and cross-modal coherence.
t3A04C8BRK.key_idea: Evaluate image, narration and speech jointly from one storybook context with cross-modal coherence rubrics, instead of scoring each modality in isolation.
t3A04C8BRK.evidence: 900 validated story transitions from openly licensed children's books, 32 baseline configurations spanning orchestration, semi-orchestration and native any-to-any paradigms, and several judge families with human ratings.
t3A04C8BRK.claimed_gains: not stated; across 32 baseline configurations, orchestration with strong VLM planning is most reliable and image generation is the clearest bottleneck.
t3A04C8BRK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the concrete cross-modal coherence task and the extensive evaluation pipeline with several judge families, human ratings and bootstrap intervals.
t3A04C8BRK.main_concern: Added value over UniM and InterleavedBench is unclear, and next-page conditions derived from the ground-truth page reduce the task to oracle-conditioned rendering with limited external validity.

2EHaQbtE4m.one_liner: Adapts large vision models for time series forecasting with a spectral magnitude aligner on rendered images and structure-guided LoRA.
2EHaQbtE4m.problem: Rendered time series images have a shallower power spectrum than natural images, and folding 1D sequences into 2D grids creates spurious adjacencies while severing temporal continuity, limiting transfer from pretrained vision models.
2EHaQbtE4m.method: SSDA is a dual-branch network. A Spectral Magnitude Aligner applies a 2D FFT to enhance the magnitude spectrum toward natural-image statistics while preserving phase, and Structural-Guided LoRA injects position-aware temporal encodings into patch embeddings and adapts attention with low-rank updates.
2EHaQbtE4m.key_idea: Enhance the FFT magnitude of rendered series images toward natural-image statistics at the data level, and inject temporal position encodings with low-rank attention updates at the model level.
2EHaQbtE4m.evidence: Several datasets and forecast horizons in full-shot and few-shot settings against recent LVM baselines, with component ablations; the abstract is cut off before the results.
2EHaQbtE4m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the examination of the spectral and structural gaps in vision-based forecasting, the small added components, and the coverage of several datasets and horizons.
2EHaQbtE4m.main_concern: The spectral-gap motivation is not tested against accuracy (SMA is trained only with the forecasting loss and the spectral slope barely moves), and branch ablations conflict between Tables 3 and 11.

ezmbV0t3L4.one_liner: Three-stage code-agent training that localizes stalled states and supervises only selected expert recovery segments for repository-level issue reproduction.
ezmbV0t3L4.problem: Imitation of code agents must identify where the student needs expert intervention and which expert behaviors correct it, but full rollouts or continuations from selected states supervise too broadly.
ezmbV0t3L4.method: LoEC shapes the initial strategy through plan-level on-policy distillation, then uses issue-reproduction progress signals to localize stalled or invalid states. For successful expert recoveries it applies intervention-level plan shaping and masked SFT over selected segments, including effective test edits retained in the final test.
ezmbV0t3L4.key_idea: Detect stalled or invalid states from issue-reproduction progress signals and apply masked SFT only to verified expert recovery segments instead of full trajectories.
ezmbV0t3L4.evidence: SWT-Bench Verified, compared with expert-takeover imitation baselines, full-trajectory BC for initial alignment, and full-suffix SFT for correction.
ezmbV0t3L4.claimed_gains: Pass@1 on SWT-Bench Verified rises from 21.11% to 32.24% after one round of stall localization and correction and to 35.06% after two, while supervised-token usage drops by over 91% and over 36% versus full-trajectory BC and full-suffix SFT.
ezmbV0t3L4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the supervision design task-aware and coherent, tying expert intervention to issue-reproduction progress, with meaningful gains over the base student.
ezmbV0t3L4.main_concern: Ablations change supervision scope, objective and recovery-plan distillation together, so the contribution of selective masked SFT is not isolated, and novelty is incremental over existing expert-correction methods.

gsPKv96g4R.one_liner: Training-free 3D reasoning segmentation: retrieve exemplar images per LLM-proposed category, lift them to point clouds, match them in the scene.
gsPKv96g4R.problem: Existing 3D reasoning segmentation systems learn from annotated scans with narrow indoor vocabularies and fail on targets outside them, because grounding rather than language is the bottleneck.
gsPKv96g4R.method: An LLM proposes candidate categories, retrieves images for each, and lifts them into point clouds. Each exemplar is placed into the query scene before encoding, matched through background-contrastive similarity maps, ranked with parameter-free distribution-calibrated scores, and verified against the retrieved images.
gsPKv96g4R.key_idea: Supply missing 3D appearance knowledge at inference by placing retrieved, lifted exemplars into the scene and matching them with background-contrastive similarity, then verifying the shortlisted masks.
gsPKv96g4R.evidence: Reason3D and the new NO-Reason3D benchmark (12 ShapeNet categories outside the training vocabulary per reviewers), compared with trained models such as Reason3D and 3D-STMN, with ablations.
gsPKv96g4R.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims it improves trained models on Reason3D without retraining and outperforms all evaluated methods on NO-Reason3D by a wide margin.
gsPKv96g4R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see inference-time retrieval to cover unseen categories without retraining as a meaningful direction, with a new out-of-vocabulary benchmark and supporting ablations.
gsPKv96g4R.main_concern: Gains are not separated from open-vocabulary 3D perception baselines, error propagation through the multi-stage LLM-retrieval pipeline is not analyzed, and accuracy on the new categories stays low.

s0hBXg4NEX.one_liner: Data-free model merging that represents each task operator as a right-singular projector scaled by a fractional inverse spectral moment.
s0hBXg4NEX.problem: Data-free merging methods that use singular structure couple singular-vector support and singular-value weighting in one spectral operator, leaving unclear how each component should be used.
s0hBXg4NEX.method: Under a covariance-weighted framework, the paper separates task support, within-support anisotropy and task-layer scale. SOS-Merge keeps right singular vectors as task support, compresses singular values into a scalar scale through a fractional inverse spectral moment, and sets the shared spectral exponent with a data-free calibration rule.
s0hBXg4NEX.key_idea: Use right singular vectors only to define task support and compress singular values into one scalar scale per task-layer, instead of direction-wise singular-value reweighting.
s0hBXg4NEX.evidence: Three CLIP ViT backbones with 8-, 14- and 20-task merging, additional RoBERTa and Qwen2.5 experiments, and a controlled Full/Scale/Shape comparison under matched support and total scale.
s0hBXg4NEX.claimed_gains: Highest average accuracy among the evaluated data-free baselines across three CLIP ViT backbones and 8-, 14-, and 20-task settings, with exponent calibration close to post-hoc grid search without few-shot data.
s0hBXg4NEX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled Full/Scale/Shape comparison convincing and the gains consistent and larger with more merged tasks, from a simple method needing no data or training.
s0hBXg4NEX.main_concern: The exponent calibration rule (matching F(q) to F(1)/K) has no clear rationale, and the notation and derivation of the objective are hard to follow.

wsfJ3c1ZGt.one_liner: Counteracts task-irrelevant signal propagation in EEG spatiotemporal graphs with a spectral graph operator motivated by stochastic PDEs.
wsfJ3c1ZGt.problem: Task-irrelevant signals propagate across electrodes and accumulate over time, entangling with predictive cues, while existing methods regularize outputs and leave the propagation process unaddressed.
wsfJ3c1ZGt.method: CounterField recasts mitigation as counteraction against propagation from a graph stochastic partial differential equation perspective. It structures a spectral response (a Matérn spectral operator per reviewers) against detrimental propagation while preserving predictive flow, with parsimony and predictive sufficiency objectives.
wsfJ3c1ZGt.key_idea: Intervene on state transitions by adding a spectral-filtered correction of temporal state differences that cancels detrimental propagation, rather than compressing the final representation.
wsfJ3c1ZGt.evidence: Diverse EEG tasks (four types per reviewers), used as a plug-in on Mamba (EvoBrain) and Transformer (CBraMod) backbones and compared with GIB and graph condensation variants.
wsfJ3c1ZGt.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports only consistent gains across EEG tasks without numbers.
wsfJ3c1ZGt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find acting on propagation rather than final representations an interesting perspective, evaluated as a plug-in across backbones and several EEG tasks.
wsfJ3c1ZGt.main_concern: The SPDE framing does not match the deterministic implementation (essentially a learnable Chebyshev graph filter on temporal differences), and there is no direct evidence that task-irrelevant propagation is actually suppressed.

JCmY9onR3T.one_liner: Adapts the flow-matching source prior and interpolation schedule per task for multi-task robot manipulation, without changing network architecture.
JCmY9onR3T.problem: Flow-based multi-task manipulation policies share one Gaussian source prior and one linear transport path across tasks, which makes tasks with distinct motion requirements hard to execute reliably.
JCmY9onR3T.method: TOPS builds multimodal task sources from reverse-mapped expert action sequences so language instructions select where generation begins. It then uses source-target covariance mismatch to slow the early transition toward expert actions and accelerate it later along directions that need expansion.
JCmY9onR3T.key_idea: Pick a task-specific multimodal source from the instruction and set a direction-dependent interpolation schedule from source-target covariance mismatch, lowering a velocity-prediction risk bound under a Gaussian endpoint model.
JCmY9onR3T.evidence: Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and CALVIN covering in-distribution, perturbation, cross-environment and data-efficiency settings, plus a Gaussian endpoint analysis and transfer to Pi 0.5 per reviewers.
JCmY9onR3T.claimed_gains: With one integration step, raises LIBERO-10 success from 53.44% to 69.67% versus ten-step Standard Flow Matching while cutting inference time to approximately one-sixth of the baseline.
JCmY9onR3T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the backbone-agnostic approach, the theory linking the schedule to velocity-prediction risk, and strong gains over flow matching baselines with faster inference.
JCmY9onR3T.main_concern: The schedule's contribution is within noise on out-of-distribution LIBERO-Plus (35.21 versus 35.29) and is confounded with a specialized solver, and the method depends on a language task selector whose errors would change the whole generation.

CtMUrUZkpO.one_liner: LLM-driven heuristic design that jointly evolves search modules and their composition, order and length as variable-length architectures.
CtMUrUZkpO.problem: Existing LLM-driven multi-operator automated heuristic design optimizes search behaviors within predefined operator organizations, which limits exploration of synergies among behaviors.
CtMUrUZkpO.method: MOSAIC represents each heuristic as an ordered, variable-length architecture of search modules. It jointly evolves modules through module rewriting and architectures through variation of module composition, execution order and architecture length.
CtMUrUZkpO.key_idea: Treat the organization of search modules (composition, order, length) as an evolvable design dimension alongside module code, using LLM module rewriting and architecture variation.
CtMUrUZkpO.evidence: Multiple multi-objective combinatorial optimization problems (three bi-objective problems plus a three-objective scheduling experiment per reviewers) against LLM-driven AHD baselines, with cross-scale generalization and module-ordering analysis.
CtMUrUZkpO.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims it outperforms advanced LLM-driven AHD methods and generalizes across scales without numbers.
CtMUrUZkpO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see explicit optimization of module organization as a well-motivated extension, backed by comprehensive experiments and an ordering analysis showing order-dependent synergy.
CtMUrUZkpO.main_concern: Novelty is seen as incremental (conventional crossover and mutation over an extended search space), the largest claimed advantage on Bi-GVRP lacks statistical significance, and computational overhead is not quantified.

U8EfcFJzKX.one_liner: Real-robot benchmark evaluating world models across passive prediction, action-conditioned modeling and action generation in one shared physical interaction space.
U8EfcFJzKX.problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate passive prediction or action-conditioned modeling separately and organize tasks semantically, so the physical interaction abilities of embodied world models stay poorly characterized.
U8EfcFJzKX.method: A three-level protocol (passive future prediction, action-conditioned world modeling, world action modeling) over tabletop manipulation organized by interaction skills and physical constraints, built on 4,500 real-robot trajectories (about 30 hours) covering 50 atomic, compositional and out-of-distribution tasks.
U8EfcFJzKX.key_idea: Organize tabletop manipulation by interaction skills and physical constraints and score the same tasks at three levels, so prediction quality can be compared with action-effect modeling and real execution.
U8EfcFJzKX.evidence: Representative world models and embodied policies (Wan and Cosmos families per reviewers) evaluated across the three levels, with cross-level correlation analysis.
U8EfcFJzKX.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports substantial variation across levels and that visually plausible prediction does not consistently give accurate action-effect modeling or robust execution.
U8EfcFJzKX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified three-level protocol and the real-robot dataset with real counterfactual outcomes for both successful and failed actions.
U8EfcFJzKX.main_concern: Cross-level conclusions rest on few, uncontrolled model families (mainly Wan and Cosmos), and the added value of the composite Level-2 score over simple task features is not shown.

G0hugVUUm9.one_liner: Wrapper for deep CTR recommenders that regularizes cross-depth representation correlation and aggregates embeddings and hidden layers through depth-specific maps.
G0hugVUUm9.problem: Making a recommender deeper does not necessarily make it better, because deeper layers need not provide distinct, useful representations.
G0hugVUUm9.method: DeCORA couples token-conditional cross-depth correlation control, a training-only objective with learned normalized pair weights, with depth-prefix aggregation. Depth-specific maps shared across sources aggregate the embedding and all hidden representations while retaining the backbone's interaction operators.
G0hugVUUm9.key_idea: Penalize correlation between representations from different depths during training and aggregate the embedding and all hidden layers through depth-specific maps so distinct responses reach the predictor.
G0hugVUUm9.evidence: Four structurally different backbones on Avazu and Criteo at Base to 16× depth, with component and parameter-matched variants, representation diagnostics, and a conditional theoretical analysis.
G0hugVUUm9.claimed_gains: Improves AUC and Logloss over vanilla in all 40 matched Base–8× configurations with a mean absolute AUC gain of 0.00156 at 8× depth, and only the full method improves mean AUC in all eight backbone–dataset pairs from 8× to 16×.
G0hugVUUm9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the depth problem in recommenders clear and relevant, with promising results on recent backbones such as DHEN and Wukong, backed by theory and many experiments.
G0hugVUUm9.main_concern: The method section and notation are hard to follow, and the evaluation is limited to two datasets (Avazu and Criteo).

d0dluhcLx4.one_liner: Builds success and failure attention prototypes from on-policy rollouts to reweight GRPO updates and token-level credit in vision-language reasoning.
d0dluhcLx4.problem: RL with verifiable rewards for vision-language models relies either on visual dependence, which does not imply correct use of visual information, or on external supervision over task-relevant image regions.
d0dluhcLx4.method: For each question, Visual Evidence Prototypes (VEPs) aggregate the attention over visual tokens of correct and incorrect rollouts into Success and Failure prototypes and contrast them. VEP-RL uses the contrast to reweight trajectory-level updates and redistribute token-level credit to the selected tokens.
d0dluhcLx4.key_idea: Contrast attention over visual tokens between correct and incorrect rollouts to find key evidence tokens, then reweight advantages and redistribute credit to those tokens without region annotations.
d0dluhcLx4.evidence: Fourteen visual reasoning and perception benchmarks across three backbones including out-of-distribution sets, plus an intervention analysis on the top 10% of visual tokens selected by VEPs.
d0dluhcLx4.claimed_gains: Improves average accuracy over the strongest baseline by 2.44, 1.93 and 3.24 absolute percentage points on three models, and intervening on the top 10% VEP visual tokens reduces accuracy by 20.15–28.45 points.
d0dluhcLx4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value obtaining fine-grained visual supervision without region annotations, supported by controls showing the prototype contrast separates correct from incorrect rollouts and by consistent gains.
d0dluhcLx4.main_concern: VEP guidance is active in only about 25% of training groups, and reviewers doubt that VEP selection rather than other recipe differences drives the gains, given fixed hyperparameters, single-run ablations and attention evidence that may be correlational.

o1WLmlRpL1.one_liner: Input-grounded benchmark scoring multi-object memory in video world models by presence, identity and structure of objects in the initial observation.
o1WLmlRpL1.problem: Existing evaluation of video world model memory relies on generated histories, video references or selected revisit viewpoints, which confounds the assessment of true memory.
o1WLmlRpL1.method: OPIS anchors evaluation to a fixed set of object instances from the initial observation, with 500 cases across real-world, embodied-robotic and game-world domains and object-level annotations for 12,672 instances. An object-centric evaluator combines association and explicit visibility reasoning to measure Object Presence, Identity and Structure on static or dynamic tracks.
o1WLmlRpL1.key_idea: Fix the reference to object instances in the input image and score each generated video for presence, identity and structure with visibility reasoning, not generated or reference video.
o1WLmlRpL1.evidence: Eight image-to-video or camera-conditioned world models, a study of reference inventory size, bootstrap intervals, and agreement with manual review per reviewers.
o1WLmlRpL1.claimed_gains: not stated as gains; OPIS scores across eight models range from 48.65 to 56.01, and average Identity falls from 40.22 to 23.11 as the object inventory grows from less than 20 to more than 40.
o1WLmlRpL1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value grounding evaluation in the input image and separating presence, identity and structure, with a large multi-domain annotated dataset.
o1WLmlRpL1.main_concern: The strict metric's validity is unclear (one below-threshold object fails a frame, the score ignores camera motion, and Presence is lenient), and the density finding may be built into the metric itself.

7ml2HPLoME.one_liner: Tuning-free framework that retrieves and verifies the event behind a visible emotion before multimodal models predict it.
7ml2HPLoME.problem: Visual emotion recognition assumes all needed evidence is in the image or video, but the same visible reaction can signal different emotions depending on events beyond the input.
7ml2HPLoME.method: The paper defines Event-Grounded Emotion Recognition (EGER) and EGER-Bench (10,052 videos and 10,734 images across 11 emotions). AffectReveal builds and independently verifies evidence-grounded event alternatives over affect-critical factors, cross-checks them against face-masked in-media facts through bidirectional atomic evidence support, and keeps the original unmasked input for the final prediction.
7ml2HPLoME.key_idea: Recover the affect-determining event, verify it by cross-checking against face-masked in-media facts with bidirectional atomic evidence support, then predict from the original unmasked input.
7ml2HPLoME.evidence: EGER-Bench with a six-annotator human study, and three downstream models across four input settings.
7ml2HPLoME.claimed_gains: Event context raises human recognition accuracy from 33.96% to 72.08%, and AffectReveal yields average UAR gains of 5.26–10.53 points across three downstream models and four input settings.
7ml2HPLoME.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the new task and large benchmark, with a human study showing that visual evidence alone is often insufficient and consistent within-model gains.
7ml2HPLoME.main_concern: Gains may come mostly from retrieving an event at all rather than from the verification framework (most recovered events are mismatches), there are no retrieval-augmented baselines, and label leakage and task novelty are questioned.

FZAUWsJD3m.one_liner: Adds new concepts to a trained concept bottleneck model with influence-style EK-FAC second-order updates and a trust region, avoiding retraining.
FZAUWsJD3m.problem: Standard concept bottleneck models have a static concept space, and expanding it normally requires full retraining that is computationally prohibitive and risks semantic drift in existing concepts.
FZAUWsJD3m.method: CABM formulates concept addition as a parameter perturbation problem solved by influence-inspired local updates. It uses EK-FAC for structured approximate second-order updates, a trust-region constraint and concept-conditional initialization, and bounds the local error relative to a re-optimized appended concept block.
FZAUWsJD3m.key_idea: Treat adding a concept as a parameter perturbation and solve it with EK-FAC approximate-curvature influence updates under a trust region, instead of end-to-end retraining.
FZAUWsJD3m.evidence: Experiments on five datasets (per reviewers) against full retraining, Probe-LR and continual CBM baselines, with concept preservation, intervention stability and sequential concept addition studies, plus a local error bound.
FZAUWsJD3m.claimed_gains: Predictive performance on par with full retraining while reducing computational cost by 10.8–61.5× relative to full retraining and 1.21–1.53× relative to a matched converged baseline (the abstract is cut off).
FZAUWsJD3m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CABM matches full-retraining accuracy while cutting update time substantially and leaving existing concept predictors unchanged.
FZAUWsJD3m.main_concern: Technical novelty is unclear next to Editable CBMs and other concept-addition work (it combines established EK-FAC, trust-region and initialization pieces), and the speedup over the frozen-feature Probe-LR baseline is only 1.2–1.5×.

elcVIsGXqC.one_liner: Post-training compression of spiking neural networks that balances inserted and deleted spikes, not just layerwise reconstruction error.
elcVIsGXqC.problem: Existing post-training compression for SNNs minimizes layerwise reconstruction error but overlooks the discrete, temporal nature of spike transmission, where weight perturbations act only through spike flips.
elcVIsGXqC.method: FastSNN jointly accounts for signal reconstruction and flip balance during compression. It models the relation between weight perturbations and spike flips in a unified form that covers pruning and quantization.
elcVIsGXqC.key_idea: Choose compression perturbations so inserted and deleted spikes stay balanced, since post-compression accuracy depends less on the number of spike flips than on their balance.
elcVIsGXqC.evidence: Multiple datasets and SNN models at high sparsity (87.5% unstructured and 2:8 structured per reviewers), with on-device evaluation on CPU and Darwin3 neuromorphic hardware.
elcVIsGXqC.claimed_gains: Outperforms the state-of-the-art method by 9.09% on average under 87.5% sparsity (the abstract is cut off after this).
elcVIsGXqC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the flip-balance motivation concrete, the gains at high sparsity substantial, and the CPU and Darwin3 hardware evaluation practically useful.
elcVIsGXqC.main_concern: The two metrics used only indirectly reflect flip balance (the method resembles existing Hessian/Fisher-guided compression), and sequential prune-then-quantize baselines and hardware measurement details are missing.

sOSbDyUXW6.one_liner: Proves that an adaptive learning rate based on accumulated prediction errors improves scaling exponents of quadratic neural networks without tuning.
sOSbDyUXW6.problem: Scaling behavior of adaptive training algorithms is poorly characterized compared with fixed-learning-rate methods, which need manual tuning.
sOSbDyUXW6.method: A theoretical analysis of scaling laws for adaptive training of quadratic neural networks, characterizing exponents by target complexity and model size for an algorithm that uses accumulated prediction errors. Empirical checks extend to general activations and practical adaptive algorithms that accumulate squared gradients.
sOSbDyUXW6.key_idea: Set the learning rate from accumulated prediction errors so that one run tracks the signal-dominated to noise-dominated transition and reaches optimal scaling exponents at any time-step.
sOSbDyUXW6.evidence: Theory for quadratic networks in a feature-learning, power-law teacher setting, plus empirical experiments with general activation functions and practical optimizers such as Adam and RMSprop.
sOSbDyUXW6.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract claims statistically optimal scaling exponents at any time-step without manual learning-rate tuning.
sOSbDyUXW6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the end-to-end risk analysis of an adaptive optimizer on a feature-learning network, in a tractable quadratic setting with near-optimal exponents.
sOSbDyUXW6.main_concern: The analyzed optimizer is one specific loss-driven schedule unlike parameter-wise adaptivity in Adam, and the noiseless scaling result needs a clearer validity range.

JP2R0TaMy1.one_liner: Forward-process RL for flow-matching 3D generation: match each negative sample to a positive target, then steer its velocity toward it.
JP2R0TaMy1.problem: DPO-, GRPO- and NFT-style objectives applied to negative trajectories only steer predicted velocities away from them without specifying a target velocity toward preferred samples, giving limited geometric gains in 3D generation.
JP2R0TaMy1.method: Dynamic Homing Optimization (DHO) reformulates negative-trajectory optimization as positive-sample attraction. Minimum-Cost Attractive Matching (MAM) assigns each negative sample a distinct positive target, and Time-Aware Dynamic Correction (TDC) redirects its trajectory with a remaining-time-aware corrective velocity. Flow3D-Pro applies asynchronous online DHO to image-to-3D geometry generation.
JP2R0TaMy1.key_idea: Give each negative sample a distinct positive target by minimum-cost matching and redirect its trajectory with a corrective velocity scaled by the remaining time.
JP2R0TaMy1.evidence: A controlled comparison of RL objectives with the same SFT initialization and reward model, comparisons with existing mesh generation methods, ablations, and a user study per reviewers.
JP2R0TaMy1.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims DHO outperforms DPO-, GRPO- and NFT-style objectives and Flow3D-Pro produces higher-quality 3D geometry without numbers.
JP2R0TaMy1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea simple and intuitive, giving negative samples explicit positive targets, and applicable to pretrained flow-matching models with gains over RL baselines.
JP2R0TaMy1.main_concern: The motivation and novelty of one-to-one matching and time-aware correction need clarifying, and evaluation lacks diversity measures, direct geometric accuracy metrics, and refinement-controlled comparisons.

Pzd6dgwKKE.one_liner: Treats KV-cache eviction and quantization as one rate-distortion bit allocation, solved per token or channel by Lagrangian relaxation.
Pzd6dgwKKE.problem: Existing methods shrink the KV cache by eviction or quantization in isolation, while long-context inference is bound by memory size and bandwidth.
Pzd6dgwKKE.method: RDKV derives each token's or channel's weight from the distortion that compression induces on the attention computation. It then assigns each a bit-width from full precision down to zero bits (eviction) through Lagrangian relaxation.
Pzd6dgwKKE.key_idea: Treat eviction as a zero-bit choice and allocate bit-widths by attention-induced distortion weights under a Lagrangian budget, so eviction and quantization are optimized jointly.
Pzd6dgwKKE.evidence: LongBench, RULER and InfiniteBench across several model families, with packed kernels, TTFT and end-to-end latency measurements, and an action-space ablation.
Pzd6dgwKKE.claimed_gains: Outperforms the best evaluated baseline by 9.1% on average, recovers 97.81% of full-cache accuracy on LongBench with only 2.48% cache retention, and gives 4.5× decode speedup and 1.9× peak memory reduction versus full-cache FlashAttention-2 decoding with 128K context (the abstract is cut off).
Pzd6dgwKKE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the rate-distortion unification of eviction and quantization clean and the gains consistent across model families and long-context benchmarks.
Pzd6dgwKKE.main_concern: Budgets match nominal bit-widths and exclude quantization metadata such as scales and zero-points, so comparisons at actual memory are missing, and the allocator is not isolated against a simple importance-ranked mixed-precision heuristic.

dahchK6UBy.one_liner: Robot self-improvement system that decomposes tasks into compound, atomic, and base skills and confines revisions to the responsible branch.
dahchK6UBy.problem: Robot agents can repair code from execution feedback, but experience is not organized around task structure, so repairs are not attributed to the responsible capability, supported by evidence, or validated before reuse.
dahchK6UBy.method: Top-Down Skill Refinement (TSR) decomposes tasks into skills with scoped responsibilities and input-output contracts and attributes each failure to a branch; a Manager, Planner, Engineer, and Reviewer coordinate planning, execution, diagnosis, and validated skill release, and stable sequences are consolidated into compound skills.
dahchK6UBy.key_idea: Attribute each execution outcome to the responsible branch of a compound-atomic-base skill hierarchy and restrict revision to that branch, releasing new skills only after validation.
dahchK6UBy.evidence: A 104-round multi-object household cleanup study on a mobile manipulator, and simulation on LIBERO, LIBERO-PRO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin.
dahchK6UBy.claimed_gains: Highest success rate on LIBERO, LIBERO-PRO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.7 to 11.0 percentage points.
dahchK6UBy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation and overall design are clear, with evaluation on four simulation benchmarks plus a long physical development study.
dahchK6UBy.main_concern: Baselines are not matched because RoboRSI keeps learning on the evaluated tasks, and gains cannot be attributed to TSR rather than other components, with TSR tested on only one failed task and two seeds.

FO92Bb6zNh.one_liner: LatFuse builds fused representations for every modality subset bottom-up on the Boolean lattice, reusing single-modality extensions as fusion units.
FO92Bb6zNh.problem: A modality's marginal contribution depends on which modalities are already present, which is equivalent to higher-order interactions, and existing fusion does not structure this context dependence.
FO92Bb6zNh.method: Fusion is formulated as a vector-valued set function over modality subsets; LatFuse constructs a fused state for each subset bottom-up on the Boolean lattice using single-modality extensions as reusable units. Since every subset state exists, it can infer on sublattices when modalities are missing.
FO92Bb6zNh.key_idea: Compute each subset's fused state from its smaller subsets plus one added modality, so local context dependence composes into global higher-order interactions.
FO92Bb6zNh.evidence: Four benchmarks with three or four modalities (multiomics classification, sentiment analysis, semantic segmentation), missing-modality tests, and synthetic tasks with known interaction structures.
FO92Bb6zNh.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest baselines on all task metrics and is more robust under most missing-modality conditions; no numbers stated.
FO92Bb6zNh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the set-function and Mobius-inversion framing gives a clear theoretical basis, and that the model can run on any observed modality subset without retraining or imputation, with strong results over baselines.
FO92Bb6zNh.main_concern: Gains may come from extra intermediate states, computational paths, or subset supervision rather than higher-order modeling, model cost grows with the number of modalities, and synthetic checks do not directly show Mobius components match true interactions.

Ti6dhMzMJ1.one_liner: Post-trains diffusion language models by minimizing MMD between generated and reference token features from a frozen pretrained DLM.
Ti6dhMzMJ1.problem: Post-training diffusion language models, including few-step generation, lacks an objective that avoids full sampling trajectories and jointly trained auxiliary models.
Ti6dhMzMJ1.method: Retains contextual features at individual token positions from a single extractor pass to estimate MMD, then optimizes with policy gradients for discrete models and direct differentiation through generated latents for continuous models.
Ti6dhMzMJ1.key_idea: Estimate MMD in a frozen pretrained DLM's feature space using per-token contextual features as multiple observations per sequence, optimized by policy gradient (discrete) or pathwise gradients (continuous).
Ti6dhMzMJ1.evidence: Experiments on OpenWebText and GSM8K, plus application to 16B DMax-LLaDA2.0 models with hybrid masked-uniform diffusion on math and code benchmarks.
Ti6dhMzMJ1.claimed_gains: Lower generative perplexity at comparable entropy on OpenWebText, better accuracy-computation trade-offs on GSM8K, and higher decoding parallelism with similar or higher accuracy on 16B DMax-LLaDA2.0 models; no numeric gains stated.
Ti6dhMzMJ1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, applicable to both discrete and continuous diffusion language models, and supported by experiments and ablations of the main design choices.
Ti6dhMzMJ1.main_concern: The link between matching token-feature distributions and better sequence-level generation is largely empirical, and the 16B runs lack a baseline continuing the original DMax objective at comparable budget.

r5V7pVAiDC.one_liner: Routes continual-learning LoRA experts using the output of the selected visual projector, so the language gate sees that projector's representation.
r5V7pVAiDC.problem: Selecting a visual expert changes the representation the language experts must process, but existing allocation does not use that dependency.
r5V7pVAiDC.method: ELGAR uses an instruction-conditioned gate to select a visual projector and a language gate that observes that projector's output to combine frozen LoRA updates, with one projector and one autoregressive path at deployment. A finite-candidate analysis characterizes when an observation supports an optimal allocation.
r5V7pVAiDC.key_idea: Feed the selected visual projector's output to the language gate that mixes frozen LoRA updates, instead of a pooled bank mean or static allocation.
r5V7pVAiDC.evidence: Three paired source-order repeats on six UCIT tasks with 3,000 examples each, matched controls, and four UCIT/DCL-backbone settings including LLaVA, compared with reproduced continual baselines.
r5V7pVAiDC.claimed_gains: 75.53 mean final average score (FAA) for selected-output routing versus 74.85 for bank-mean routing and 73.75 for static allocation, and complete ELGAR reaches 75.63 FAA on UCIT-LLaVA.
r5V7pVAiDC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing the selected projector's output to the language allocator is an intuitive design and that the complete system performs strongly with a solid experimental study.
r5V7pVAiDC.main_concern: The method mostly improves routing features on existing projector selection and LoRA routing, and it is unclear how much of the gain over baselines comes from ELGAR versus other design choices.

QtyjAoodAd.one_liner: Mixture-of-charts VAE where chart assignment is posterior inference with latent-evidence routing, then recovers an atlas from the charts.
QtyjAoodAd.problem: A single global latent coordinate system cannot represent a complex data manifold without distortion, and deciding which chart handles which point without labels is usually heuristic.
QtyjAoodAd.method: Variational Atlas Autoencoders treat the chart index as a latent variable, so the evidence lower bound gives the training objective and chart assignment becomes posterior inference. Latent-evidence routing assigns a point to a chart in proportion to the evidence of its encoding under that chart's latent prior, and an atlas is recovered from the trained charts.
QtyjAoodAd.key_idea: Route each point to a chart in proportion to the evidence of its encoding under that chart's latent prior, so assignment depends on the encoder alone and is self-supervised.
QtyjAoodAd.evidence: Unsupervised chart discovery that separates classes and subclasses (shoes, faces), with sample FID comparisons against VaDE on CelebA and Fashion-MNIST and interpolation examples mentioned in reviews.
QtyjAoodAd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning local latent charts without supervision is meaningful and that the simple latent-evidence routing rule is a principled alternative to reconstruction-based assignment.
QtyjAoodAd.main_concern: The contribution over earlier atlas and chart-autoencoder models is unclear, FID gains are small relative to variation, and the closest multi-chart baselines were excluded after training failures.

zlr69HxVP2.one_liner: Maps six training-derived task statistics to a block-wise positive-definite metric that preconditions forecasting model optimization.
zlr69HxVP2.problem: It is unclear whether a forecasting task's characteristics can inform how its model is optimized without changing the forecasting architecture.
