zlr69HxVP2.method: ROAM maps six training-derived task statistics to a block-wise positive-definite metric. A slow population controller adapts the metric, and a two-signal transition switches between momentum-based and quasi-Newton updates.
zlr69HxVP2.key_idea: Task statistics set a block-wise Riemannian preconditioning metric, adapted by a slow population controller and a switch from momentum to quasi-Newton updates.
zlr69HxVP2.evidence: Seven datasets and five backbones, four matched-budget optimizer comparisons, a three-component factorial ablation, and a local analysis relating metric alignment and cross-block coupling to conditioning.
zlr69HxVP2.claimed_gains: Improves all 35 dataset-backbone MSE aggregates relative to standard training recipes, with approximately 4.8%-7.3% lower macro-average MSE by backbone.
zlr69HxVP2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning the optimizer on task statistics is an interesting perspective, with broad and relatively consistent experiments and ablations.
zlr69HxVP2.main_concern: The mapping from task statistics to the metric (the W and b parameters, curvature proxy) is under-explained, and the theory does not show that these statistics satisfy the alignment conditions.

sZSUvOrJZv.one_liner: Treats Koopman rollout predictions as noisy latent states and corrects them with a pretrained flow-matching model for long-horizon PDE emulation.
sZSUvOrJZv.problem: Learned finite-dimensional Koopman representations are only approximately invariant, so unresolved dynamics and closure errors accumulate and extrapolation beyond the training horizon remains challenging.
sZSUvOrJZv.method: KoopFlow is a prediction-correction framework in which a linear Koopman model predicts latent states and a pretrained flow-matching model acts as a probabilistic transport bridge toward the target latent distribution, treating accumulated Koopman error as progressive distributional degradation.
sZSUvOrJZv.key_idea: Reinterpret Koopman error accumulation as distributional degradation and apply flow matching to transport degraded latent predictions back to the target latent distribution.
sZSUvOrJZv.evidence: Experiments across diverse PDE benchmarks (four 2D benchmarks per reviewers), including forecasts beyond the training horizon, and ablations of the generative correction.
sZSUvOrJZv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the long-horizon, temporally out-of-distribution performance is strong and the dual-pathway motivation is intuitive, with ablations showing that generative correction improves the Koopman model.
sZSUvOrJZv.main_concern: The theory is disconnected from the implementation (Stage II trains a standard flow-matching objective without the degradation distribution or Koopman operator), and the Mori-Zwanzig link and Gaussian assumption are weakly supported.

QcCZA9gmq6.one_liner: Benchmark grounded in Belbin team-role theory evaluating LLMs on 9 team roles in a constrained-adaptive multi-party collaboration simulator.
QcCZA9gmq6.problem: Existing collaboration evaluations of LLMs are constrained to specific tasks, roles, or interaction paradigms, leaving broader team responsibilities and dynamic multi-party collaboration insufficiently characterized.
QcCZA9gmq6.method: CoMateEval covers 9 team roles through 18 collaborative scenarios instantiated as 370 evaluation cases. CoMateSim is a simulator where predefined event structures and branch conditions govern progression while trajectories evolve with model behavior, and models are scored by rubric on how well they fulfill their assigned responsibilities.
QcCZA9gmq6.key_idea: Score LLMs on fulfilling an assigned Belbin team-role responsibility inside an event-branching simulator, rather than on isolated task success.
QcCZA9gmq6.evidence: Experiments on frontier LLMs across the selected scenarios.
QcCZA9gmq6.claimed_gains: The strongest model achieves an average rubric pass rate of 45.47% across the selected scenarios.
QcCZA9gmq6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating responsibility fulfillment across nine team roles is a meaningful, underexplored target, with clear writing and a reasonable experimental design.
QcCZA9gmq6.main_concern: Novelty over prior social-simulation benchmarks such as Sotopia is unclear, and a GPT-5.5 backend serves as simulator, scheduler, and judge while also being an evaluated model.

Yaa0SazX4c.one_liner: Injects a teacher's insight at a chosen restart turn when all GRPO attempts fail, stripping it before the update.
Yaa0SazX4c.problem: With few training tasks, most GRPO groups are all-fail and give no gradient, and existing hint methods study single-turn reasoning where hints can only go in the prompt.
Yaa0SazX4c.method: When every attempt fails, a teacher chooses a restart turn, reads the reference solution, and writes an insight explaining how to find the answer; the policy retries from that turn. The insight is removed before the update so the update sees the same inputs as at evaluation.
Yaa0SazX4c.key_idea: Place a teacher-written insight at a teacher-chosen mid-trajectory turn for dead groups, then strip it from the context before computing the policy update.
Yaa0SazX4c.evidence: AppWorld (90 tasks) and TravelPlanner (45 queries) at 4B and 9B scales, with ablations on hint placement and stripping.
Yaa0SazX4c.claimed_gains: Over GRPO at 4B and 9B, AppWorld Test-Challenge scenario goal completion improves by 13.2 and 9.2 points and TravelPlanner leaderboard test success by 29.1 and 4.5.
Yaa0SazX4c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method targets a practical problem of all-fail groups in data-scarce multi-turn agent RL, is simple, and shows solid gains over vanilla GRPO with ablations on hint placement and stripping.
Yaa0SazX4c.main_concern: Novelty over existing hint and turn-level restart methods is limited, placement ablations confound hint location with content, and the cost of frequent large-teacher calls is not analyzed.

LcI2183vpR.one_liner: Post-trains a pretrained humanoid behavior foundation model to recover from falls without adding parameters, while preserving motion tracking.
LcI2183vpR.problem: Pretrained behavior foundation models track reference motions well from small state-reference discrepancies but cannot recover from falls, and adding recovery must preserve tracking at low training overhead.
LcI2183vpR.method: Frames recovery as extending the effective closed-loop control range of a pretrained BFM across discrepancy regimes, treating tracking and recovery as one state-reference conditional decoding problem, and applies simple low-overhead post-training without adding model parameters (abstract truncated). Reviewers describe expert supervision through DAgger with asynchronous PPO and behavior-cloning updates.
LcI2183vpR.key_idea: Extend a pretrained tracking decoder to large state-reference discrepancies by post-training with a recovery expert, keeping the deployed decoder and control interface unchanged.
LcI2183vpR.evidence: Humanoid tracking and recovery evaluation on AMASS and Motion Decode, with a real-world G1 deployment, according to reviews (abstract truncated).
LcI2183vpR.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; reviewers cite 93.2% eventual stand-up success and 73.6% motion recovery for the MLP versus zero recovery for the pretrained tracker.
LcI2183vpR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is practical and that the method adds substantial fall recovery to a pretrained tracker without a separate recovery controller or extra deployed capacity.
LcI2183vpR.main_concern: Gains are not isolated from expert supervision (no simpler PPO plus BC baselines), and tracking success drops on Motion Decode from 82.38% to 76.85% while real-world recovery is not quantified.

r9wVbCY0Z0.one_liner: Generates rules with an LLM using relation memory, a KG tokenizer, and a neuro-symbolic reasoner for knowledge graph reasoning.
r9wVbCY0Z0.problem: KG structural context and LLM parametric knowledge are represented inconsistently, so LLMs perceive reasoning evidence poorly and reasoning loses effectiveness and faithfulness (called reasoning evidence perception drift).
r9wVbCY0Z0.method: A Structure-Internalized Rule Generator uses an in-context learning block with a structural relation memory, plus a KG tokenizer based on structural invariance learning and a neuro-symbolic reasoner (cut off in the abstract). Reviews say generated rule representations are incorporated into NBFNet.
r9wVbCY0Z0.key_idea: Couple parametric learning of structural knowledge with faithfulness evaluation of reasoning by generating rules anchored to KG structure through a relation memory.
r9wVbCY0Z0.evidence: Experiments on 36 datasets against 17 baselines including inductive settings, with ablations, backbone comparisons, and efficiency breakdowns as described in reviews.
r9wVbCY0Z0.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the TL;DR claims strong performance across 36 datasets.
r9wVbCY0Z0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the practical bottleneck addressed, the combination of rule generation, relational memory, and neuro-symbolic reasoning, and the experimental breadth of 36 datasets and 17 baselines.
r9wVbCY0Z0.main_concern: How reasoning faithfulness is guaranteed or quantitatively evaluated is unclear, and novelty over ULTRA, MOTIF, KRLM, and ChatRule is not clearly established.

yaVsz4fH7K.one_liner: Normalized pseudogradient dynamics driven by one-bit pairwise comparisons give ordinal regret and Nash guarantees in continuous games.
yaVsz4fH7K.problem: With only pairwise preference feedback, standard external regret and coarse correlated equilibria are not identifiable: ordinally equivalent games can yield zero regret in one and linear regret in the other for the same play.
yaVsz4fH7K.method: The paper defines an ordinal directional regret benchmark from normalized unilateral preference directions and shows block-normalized pseudogradient dynamics achieve sublinear ordinal regret. A one-bit comparison estimator implements the dynamics with one comparison per player and round.
yaVsz4fH7K.key_idea: Replace cardinal gradients with normalized unilateral preference directions estimated from one-bit comparisons, so regret and equilibrium notions depend only on ordinal information.
yaVsz4fH7K.evidence: Theoretical results: non-identifiability of external regret and CCE, sublinear ordinal regret, and almost-sure last-iterate convergence to the Nash set in ordinal potential games; no experiments are visible in the abstract text provided.
yaVsz4fH7K.claimed_gains: not stated (the guarantees are qualitative: sublinear finite-resolution ordinal regret and last-iterate convergence to the Nash set in ordinal potential games).
yaVsz4fH7K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the well-motivated preference-only setting, the identifiability results that expose a gap in no-regret theory, and the regret and convergence guarantees.
yaVsz4fH7K.main_concern: Limited technical novelty: the regret and convergence theorems appear to follow from standard projected online gradient descent analysis, so the contribution reads as mostly framing.

n92Fgk1rH4.one_liner: IDScore adds a bounded task-conditioned likelihood residual to surrogate gradients in low-bit quantization-aware training.
n92Fgk1rH4.problem: Deterministic quantization is piecewise constant, so QAT relies on surrogate gradients whose quality limits effective training.
n92Fgk1rH4.method: IDScore builds a local likelihood score from a task-selected neighboring target, the latent parameter, and the quantization thresholds, and uses it as a bounded residual correction to the surrogate gradient, inspired by quantized system identification.
n92Fgk1rH4.key_idea: Exploit the quantizer's threshold structure through a target-conditioned ordinal likelihood score used as a bounded residual on the surrogate gradient.
n92Fgk1rH4.evidence: Vision and language experiments, including QuEST-30M W2A2 perplexity and combination with CAGE, plus theorems on target-direction consistency and likelihood allocation; reviews note AdamW and Muon dynamics in Table 4.
n92Fgk1rH4.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a review cites QuEST-30M W2A2 validation perplexity improving from 37.262 to 36.502.
n92Fgk1rH4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives consistent gains over QAT baselines such as QuEST and CAGE across vision and language tasks at small extra cost (about 2% step time and 0.4% memory).
n92Fgk1rH4.main_concern: The evidence does not show the full ordinal likelihood is needed, since a simpler Boundary-NLL control recovers most of the gain (36.611 versus 36.502 perplexity), and the theory does not cover the AdamW or Muon dynamics that were evaluated.

0hAEdPHSkE.one_liner: RefBeliefMap models spatial and semantic evidence uncertainty and triggers active observation before committing in zero-shot object navigation.
0hAEdPHSkE.problem: ZSON methods built on LLMs and VLMs do not address whether available evidence supports a navigation choice, nor how new evidence changes the search value of previously visited locations.
0hAEdPHSkE.method: RefBeliefMap separates target-location belief from spatial and semantic evidence uncertainty, estimated from intra-observation uncertainty and inter-observation disagreement over a sliding memory window, and triggers active observation and semantic reasoning when frontiers are unresolved. RefBeliefNav jointly scores unexplored frontiers and historical waypoints by target-finding potential, expected information gain, and navigation cost.
0hAEdPHSkE.key_idea: Estimate evidence reliability from intra-observation uncertainty and inter-observation disagreement, refine beliefs when frontiers are unresolved, and rank frontiers and past waypoints under one objective.
0hAEdPHSkE.evidence: Zero-shot navigation experiments (details cut off in the abstract); reviews cite a frontier-only ablation (64.6 versus 69.5 SR) and BLIP-2 scores plus a multimodal LLM as evidence sources.
0hAEdPHSkE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of checking evidence reliability before committing, and treating revisitation as a regular decision, intuitive and well motivated, with an efficient adaptive trigger.
0hAEdPHSkE.main_concern: The uncertainty estimates are never shown to be calibrated or to track real evidence errors, and the belief fusion assumes conditionally independent observations although consecutive frames are highly correlated.

wP3ou7tnlZ.one_liner: Trains a lightweight predictor to estimate cross-model neighborhood disagreement from a single model's representation.
wP3ou7tnlZ.problem: Prior work measures representation disagreement across foundation models using multiple representation sets, while predicting disagreement from a single representation for input reliability estimation is unexplored.
wP3ou7tnlZ.method: Quantifies disagreement by comparing each sample's nearest neighbors across different models' representation spaces, then trains a lightweight predictor that estimates it from a single model's representation at inference time.
wP3ou7tnlZ.key_idea: Define disagreement as cross-model nearest-neighbor agreement, then learn to predict it from one model's representation alone.
wP3ou7tnlZ.evidence: Experiments across diverse foundation models and datasets show disagreement is input-dependent, predictable, and generalizable; reviews mention leave-anchor-out results.
wP3ou7tnlZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the extensive experiments show a single model's representation carries information about cross-model disagreement, though their ratings differ widely (1, 4, and 3).
wP3ou7tnlZ.main_concern: The technical contribution is weak and heuristic: the neighborhood-agreement score and top-k construction have precedents, the ground truth is self-defined, and the motivation for predicting disagreement is unclear.

ZAVR1xh41K.one_liner: Low-resolution structural and density priors constrain Gaussian expansion to defend 3D splatting against computation-cost attacks.
ZAVR1xh41K.problem: Image purification can erase valid textures while failing to control attack-induced abnormal Gaussian geometry and spatial congestion.
ZAVR1xh41K.method: CAGE-GS combines mild wavelet denoising with low-resolution reconstruction to obtain structural and density priors. During full-resolution optimization, these priors reject implausible Gaussian candidates and suppress excessive local expansion.
ZAVR1xh41K.key_idea: Use low-resolution geometry and density priors to reject anomalous Gaussian candidates and cap local expansion during full-resolution training.
ZAVR1xh41K.evidence: Experiments span three benchmark datasets, different Gaussian-splatting implementations including Mip-Splatting, and multiple perturbation budgets and hyperparameter settings.
ZAVR1xh41K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent resource savings and better preservation of clean-input reconstruction quality than compared defenses.
ZAVR1xh41K.main_concern: All reviewers flag the lack of adaptive attacks targeting downsampling or corruption of the low-resolution priors.

PNazQQH6kv.one_liner: Reusable temporal snapshots and global heuristics test how much heavyweight modeling contributes to future graph-link prediction.
PNazQQH6kv.problem: Temporal text-attributed graph link predictors incur high computational costs without clearly separating the value of historical evidence from model complexity.
PNazQQH6kv.method: The paper evaluates a lightweight Snapshot GNN using reusable temporal snapshots and inexpensive global heuristics. It derives a conditional AUC bound for compressed additive history summaries and uses controlled comparisons to examine history granularity, processing complexity, and uncertainty-localized LLM benefits.
PNazQQH6kv.key_idea: Compress interaction history into reusable snapshots and separate the effects of available evidence, graph processing, and LLM assistance.
PNazQQH6kv.evidence: Experiments cover four TTAG benchmarks in transductive and inductive settings, alongside a conditional theoretical bound on the full-history AUC advantage.
PNazQQH6kv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize that the lightweight approach achieves competitive link-prediction performance with substantially lower computational cost.
PNazQQH6kv.main_concern: Reviewers question how the conditional theoretical bound applies to the implemented Snapshot GNN and whether its assumptions hold in practice.

rzt41FUGvf.one_liner: Shared-scene simulation exposes reset-frequency failures when reinforcement learning fine-tunes pretrained vision-language-action policies.
rzt41FUGvf.problem: Frequent scene resets require substantial human intervention, while non-episodic fine-tuning of large pretrained robot policies remains underexplored.
rzt41FUGvf.method: CRONOS benchmarks VLA reinforcement-learning fine-tuning under non-episodic scene resets in shared-scene multi-task physics simulation. It analyzes object-configuration and end-effector shifts and tests targeted reset allocation and corrections to pretrained-policy biases.
rzt41FUGvf.key_idea: Let scene state accumulate across tasks while varying reset allocation to expose and mitigate pretrained-policy distribution shifts.
rzt41FUGvf.evidence: Simulation experiments evaluate OpenVLA-7B and SpatialVLA-4B with PPO across four tabletop scenes and sixteen manipulation tasks, including unseen configurations and task sequences.
rzt41FUGvf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reset burden is a practical obstacle and that studying pretrained VLA behavior under infrequent resets is useful.
rzt41FUGvf.main_concern: Reviewers repeatedly criticize narrow benchmark coverage limited to a small set of tabletop pick-and-place tasks and policies.

lETRcTnrUb.one_liner: Alternating solution and self-refinement GRPO steps jointly train reasoning and revision under binary correctness rewards.
lETRcTnrUb.problem: Prompt-only self-refinement is brittle, while training-based alternatives often require critique annotations or signals about initial-answer correctness.
lETRcTnrUb.method: ThinkTwice replaces every even GRPO step with a refinement step on the model's solutions from the preceding step. Both stages use the same binary correctness reward without critique data or initial-correctness hints.
lETRcTnrUb.key_idea: Alternate GRPO solution generation with reward-based revision of the immediately preceding solutions.
lETRcTnrUb.evidence: Experiments cover five mathematical reasoning benchmarks and Qwen3-4B and Olmo3-7B, comparing initial answers and self-refinement with online policy-optimization baselines.
lETRcTnrUb.claimed_gains: Training takes only 3% longer than GRPO, while Qwen3-4B AIME performance exceeds GRPO by 5 percentage points before refinement and 11.5 points after one refinement step.
lETRcTnrUb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple, low-overhead training recipe and its self-refinement gains without external critique supervision.
lETRcTnrUb.main_concern: Reviewers identify missing controlled ablations and strong trained self-correction comparisons, making the source of the gains difficult to isolate.

CW8qBrc64E.one_liner: Reference-energy Feynman-Kac corrections repair diffusion-path tracking and endpoint mismatch during inference-time sampling.
CW8qBrc64E.problem: Increasing particle counts reduces Monte Carlo error but cannot repair errors inherited from imperfect pretrained diffusion models.
CW8qBrc64E.method: EBFKC derives dynamics that track prescribed probability paths in the continuous-time population limit and approximates them with guided sequential Monte Carlo. It uses pretrained energy along the path and progressively incorporates the learned-to-target terminal-energy discrepancy.
CW8qBrc64E.key_idea: Use reference-energy discrepancies in Feynman-Kac particle dynamics to correct probability-path tracking and terminal-distribution mismatch.
CW8qBrc64E.evidence: Theory and experiments examine Gaussian mixtures, particle systems, alanine dipeptide, and alanine tetrapeptide under annealing and reward tilting.
CW8qBrc64E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate distinguishing model-induced sampling errors and testing their correction in controlled and molecular settings.
CW8qBrc64E.main_concern: Reviewers question the breadth of applicability because the method requires energy-based diffusion models and a reference energy, with extension to standard score-based models unclear.

9cKlnIMZJ4.one_liner: Matched source-image and wireless-signal triggers jointly activate a cross-domain semantic-communication backdoor.
9cKlnIMZJ4.problem: Single-domain backdoor studies overlook attacks whose activation conditions span source inputs and wireless channels.
9cKlnIMZJ4.method: XComBo pairs a learnable source-domain pattern with a frequency-structured wireless signal and jointly optimizes them on a surrogate model. Energy constraints preserve benign behavior when triggers are incomplete, and the framework extends to multiple targets.
9cKlnIMZJ4.key_idea: Split backdoor activation across matched source and wireless sub-triggers coordinated by surrogate-model optimization.
9cKlnIMZJ4.evidence: Image-reconstruction experiments cover three semantic-communication systems, four datasets, communication conditions, and ablations.
9cKlnIMZJ4.claimed_gains: XComBo reports an average PSNR improvement of 12.47 dB over the strongest baseline under backdoor activation.
9cKlnIMZJ4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the motivated source-wireless attack setting and the evaluation of cross-domain paired triggers across systems.
9cKlnIMZJ4.main_concern: Reviewers question the added contribution of joint optimization because random or decoupled paired triggers already achieve strong attack performance.

2LIFTLuqHw.one_liner: Randomly shifting preceding-context RoPE key positions during unstructured passage editing reduces context reliance and improves atomic-fact recall.
2LIFTLuqHw.problem: Unstructured knowledge editing on multi-fact passages suffers from context reliance, where edited LLMs reproduce the full passage yet fail to recall individual atomic facts without the original passage context.
2LIFTLuqHw.method: FOVEATED creates focused views of each sentence during passage editing by randomly shifting the Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) positions assigned to keys in its preceding context. Removing this perturbation after editing leaves native inference positional encodings intact while reducing reliance on preceding passage tokens.
2LIFTLuqHw.key_idea: Randomly shift RoPE key positions of preceding context tokens when editing each sentence in a passage to counter context-induced difficulty underestimation.
2LIFTLuqHw.evidence: Evaluated as a plug-and-play wrapper across five editing methods, two LLM families, and three unstructured knowledge-editing benchmarks.
2LIFTLuqHw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a practical failure mode in unstructured knowledge editing and consistently improves atomic-fact recall across multiple base editors without atomic QA supervision.
2LIFTLuqHw.main_concern: Reviewers argue that lower pre-edit losses at later passage positions do not conclusively establish causal context reliance, and note missing simpler context-reduction baselines plus partial declines on general capabilities.

7hYanTUsrh.one_liner: Hadamard boundary variation converts task-defined tolerance regions into parameter-space directions for evaluating metric-learning updates.
7hYanTUsrh.problem: Pointwise ranking and comparison hardness do not directly characterize whether metric-learning updates expand task-acceptable predictions.
7hYanTUsrh.method: The framework measures the region of acceptable hypotheses that outrank every unacceptable alternative. Hadamard's first-variation formula yields the steepest first-order expansion direction and connects it to region formation, allowing comparisons and loss aggregations to be assessed against task utility.
7hYanTUsrh.key_idea: Differentiate the extent of task-correct winning regions through their competitive boundaries to derive task-directed parameter updates.
7hYanTUsrh.evidence: Theoretical derivations and empirical analyses on real-world datasets connect regional expansion with task performance.
7hYanTUsrh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the geometric formulation linking task-defined correctness regions to metric-learning comparisons and downstream performance.
7hYanTUsrh.main_concern: Reviewers question generality because the theory assumes regular competitive boundaries and differentiable, locally stable strongest unacceptable competitors.

rdUaXKFTeA.one_liner: Mirror Learning transforms third-person video into first-person trajectories and infers learner actions for behavior cloning.
rdUaXKFTeA.problem: Behavior cloning depends on aligned first-person demonstrations and cannot directly exploit abundant passive third-person observations.
rdUaXKFTeA.method: A fine-tuned video diffusion model transforms demonstrator observations into the learner's perspective, and an inverse dynamics model infers actions in the learner's control space. The resulting mirror data train policies alone or augment first-person behavior cloning.
rdUaXKFTeA.key_idea: Compose learned viewpoint transformation with inverse dynamics to convert passive third-person demonstrations into pseudo first-person action trajectories.
rdUaXKFTeA.evidence: CARLA and Minecraft experiments show policy learning from mirror data and improvements when mirror data augment first-person behavior cloning.
rdUaXKFTeA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find converting third-person videos into actionable imitation data a useful and practical application of generative world models.
rdUaXKFTeA.main_concern: Reviewers question the faithfulness of generated viewpoints because hallucinated or missing actors can distort the interactions used for policy training.

oUAcFcgA7H.one_liner: BELIEF learns outcome-conditioned evidence distributions and accumulates likelihoods to recover evolving Bayesian beliefs without intermediate probability labels.
oUAcFcgA7H.problem: Intermediate probabilities of eventual outcomes remain unobserved even after final outcomes become known.
oUAcFcgA7H.method: BELIEF models each arriving event conditional on a candidate outcome and the full preceding history. Accumulated log likelihoods and Bayesian inference produce binary, multiclass, or continuous belief paths with per-event evidence contributions.
oUAcFcgA7H.key_idea: Learn how evidence arrives under each outcome, then update outcome beliefs through accumulated conditional likelihoods.
oUAcFcgA7H.evidence: Recovery bounds and exact recovery under correct priors and evidence models accompany synthetic streams with known posterior paths and real-data reference-path comparisons.
oUAcFcgA7H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear framework and explicit explanation of how incoming evidence changes outcome beliefs.
oUAcFcgA7H.main_concern: A reviewer flags the missing temporal-consistency training baseline, leaving the advantage over objectives designed for evolving predictions unresolved.

jC6xh3GxMI.one_liner: ReCAST allocates each diffusion reward across timesteps using discriminability gains while preserving reward budgets and equal step totals.
jC6xh3GxMI.problem: Multi-reward diffusion tuning conflates how much users value each reward with when that reward becomes informative during denoising.
jC6xh3GxMI.method: ReCAST constructs a reward-by-timestep weight matrix whose row sums match user reward budgets and whose column sums assign equal total weight to denoising steps. It allocates weights according to per-step Rényi discriminability gains that telescope across denoising.
jC6xh3GxMI.key_idea: Allocate reward credit by temporal discriminability gains subject to fixed per-reward budgets and equal total weight at each timestep.
jC6xh3GxMI.evidence: Experiments train SD3.5-Medium in two four-reward settings across five budgets, with reviews noting three seeds and held-out judges.
jC6xh3GxMI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit separation between reward preference budgets and informative denoising timesteps.
jC6xh3GxMI.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the implemented surrogate supports the claimed Rényi and KL divergence interpretation of temporal credit assignment.

XCfoA1opfB.one_liner: R2GT gates federated graph transfer by validation risk and restores client checkpoints when candidate updates violate tolerance.
XCfoA1opfB.problem: Harmful cross-client transfer can persist in predictors and shared representations even after later transfer losses are downweighted.
XCfoA1opfB.method: R2GT combines semantic and structural sharing with client-specific validation acceptance, recoverable checkpoints, and cooldown-based re-entry. Clients retain acceptable candidates or restore a stored reference, with empirical validation control and conditional population-risk extensions.
XCfoA1opfB.key_idea: Make transfer effects reversible by validating candidate client states and restoring checkpoints before allowing transfer to resume after cooldown.
XCfoA1opfB.evidence: Experiments span homophilic and heterophilic graphs with disjoint and overlapping partitions, including paired rollback-versus-mask-only analyses.
XCfoA1opfB.claimed_gains: R2GT improves average performance over FedSSA in all four evaluation groups, and recovery improves next-round performance in 86.0–91.4% of rollback events.
XCfoA1opfB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value controlling the persistence of transfer through a practical combination of validation gates, checkpoint recovery, and cooldown.
XCfoA1opfB.main_concern: Reviewers flag inconsistencies between the stated recovery algorithm, reported validation violations, and rollback counts.

YvOAXhhj3H.one_liner: GAVEL orients multi-LLM aggregation with verified labels, freezes the policy, and certifies risk through fresh sequential audits.
YvOAXhhj3H.problem: Agreement among LLM evaluators can reflect correlated errors rather than factual correctness, and unlabeled interaction cannot resolve semantic orientation.
YvOAXhhj3H.method: The paper separates external facts, evaluators' private states, and peer transcripts to derive information limits for consensus evaluation. GAVEL fits and orients an aggregation policy using verified labels, freezes it, and applies an anytime-valid adaptive audit that returns a risk certificate or declines certification.
YvOAXhhj3H.key_idea: Use independently verified labels to orient a fixed aggregation policy, then allocate fresh audit evidence across task strata for risk certification.
YvOAXhhj3H.evidence: Information-theoretic bounds and audit-allocation analysis accompany synthetic and semi-synthetic studies plus real LLM evaluations on MMLU, HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge, and WinoGrande.
YvOAXhhj3H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the relevance of correlated evaluator errors and the rigorous theoretical treatment of consensus limits and auditing.
YvOAXhhj3H.main_concern: Reviewers find the advance over established statistical results and simpler local audit allocation insufficiently demonstrated.

t2eMWcoqTO.one_liner: LongCoref-AV tests whether models connect faces, voices, and actions to the same person across distant video moments.
t2eMWcoqTO.problem: Recognizing video content does not establish correct attribution of distant speech and actions to individual people.
t2eMWcoqTO.method: LongCoref-AV provides human-verified multiple-choice questions whose identity cues and evidence span distant moments, with distractors drawn largely from the same video. Identity-link labels, modality controls, evidence restriction, and separate identity-pair tests probe failure modes beyond aggregate question accuracy.
t2eMWcoqTO.key_idea: Require questions to link two voices, two faces, or a face and voice across time, then contrast question answering with direct identity matching.
t2eMWcoqTO.evidence: The benchmark contains 572 questions from 450 long-form videos and evaluates 17 systems with text-only, modality, and identity-matching controls.
t2eMWcoqTO.claimed_gains: Across 17 systems, frontier models reach 80–86% and the strongest open models 69–72%, while the two strongest open omni models mislabel more than half of different-person pairs as the same person in a separate test.
t2eMWcoqTO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value studying person attribution in long videos and using complementary diagnostics beyond aggregate question accuracy.
t2eMWcoqTO.main_concern: Reviewers question whether question accuracy measures identity coreference because substantial text-only and option-based shortcuts remain.

2vX7UBSqne.one_liner: RoboRSI evolves explicit rules for choosing and reviewing robot improvements using historical outcomes and held-out downstream validation.
2vX7UBSqne.problem: Improving a robot's execution system alone does not preserve guidance for selecting and evaluating future modifications.
2vX7UBSqne.method: RoboRSI maintains a system-level strategy that selects and reviews changes to planning guidance and robot skills. Historical traces connect decisions to their outcomes, and candidate strategies are validated through the downstream improvements they induce on held-out cases.
2vX7UBSqne.key_idea: Learn persistent modification-selection and review rules from prior outcomes, then update those rules based on held-out downstream robot improvements.
2vX7UBSqne.evidence: Four robotic benchmarks include matched-history ablations on LIBERO-Pro and comparisons between continually updated and fixed strategies on RoboCasa365.
2vX7UBSqne.claimed_gains: RoboRSI reports average task-success improvement of 15.4 percentage over no strategy, 8.2 percentage from maintaining strategy with matched history on LIBERO-Pro, and 10.6 percentage from updating rather than fixing strategy on RoboCasa365.
2vX7UBSqne.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating improvement strategy from execution and the matched-history and frozen-strategy controls.
2vX7UBSqne.main_concern: Reviewers find the connection between the claimed review mechanism and evaluated implementation unclear because the released backend does not directly dispatch PreCritic or Auditor.

LgtyXXbRfC.one_liner: AbsorbKV jointly selects retained cache states and learns carrier-conditioned writes for compatible evicted information.
LgtyXXbRfC.problem: KV-cache merging fails when retained states cannot preserve evicted information without corrupting their original contents.
LgtyXXbRfC.method: AbsorbKV's Hybrid Selector retains states based on both importance and absorbability relative to retained carriers. Adaptive Absorption routes evicted states to compatible retained states and learns value adaptation for the unchanged keys through which future queries retrieve them.
LgtyXXbRfC.key_idea: Choose cache carriers using importance and absorbability, then adapt merged information to each carrier's fixed retrieval key.
LgtyXXbRfC.evidence: Reviews describe evaluation across three models, multiple context lengths and cache budgets, two benchmarks including RULER, and selection-writer ablations.
LgtyXXbRfC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retained-state selection constrains merging quality and provides a clear reason to design selection and writing together.
LgtyXXbRfC.main_concern: Reviewers find that the selection scores and ablations do not sufficiently isolate improved carrier compatibility as the source of the gains.

dGpEyPbJNt.one_liner: Node–edge policy factorization separates route ordering from parallel-edge selection for scalable multigraph routing.
dGpEyPbJNt.problem: Neural vehicle-routing methods largely target Euclidean or simple graphs, while existing multigraph methods scale poorly.
dGpEyPbJNt.method: NEPF splits routing into node permutation and edge selection, using pre-encoding edge aggregation and a non-autoregressive edge architecture. Hierarchical reinforcement learning jointly trains the two stages.
dGpEyPbJNt.key_idea: Aggregate parallel edges before encoding and factor the routing policy into a node sequence and a separate edge-selection stage.
dGpEyPbJNt.evidence: Experiments span six VRP variants, multiple multigraph distributions, larger instances, real road networks, and different backbones.
dGpEyPbJNt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit faster training or inference while maintaining solution quality across multiple routing settings.
dGpEyPbJNt.main_concern: Comparisons do not adequately establish the value of the learned decomposition against broader neural solvers or classical edge-selection alternatives.

2hv9iSTRak.one_liner: Agent-issued cache dropping and key repositioning manage context through a history-aware KV serving engine.
2hv9iSTRak.problem: Editing an agent's token history invalidates downstream KV states and forces expensive re-prefilling of retained context.
2hv9iSTRak.method: Cache engineering exposes drop and repos operations for excluding cached states and changing retained-key position encodings. The AKV serving engine tracks operation history to reuse caches correctly behind a stateless API.
2hv9iSTRak.key_idea: Expose direct KV drop and key-position edits while matching cache reuse against operation history rather than token prefixes alone.
2hv9iSTRak.evidence: Reviews discuss agent-task accuracy comparisons, context-policy settings, API-cost estimates, and serving experiments in memory-constrained regimes.
2hv9iSTRak.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a real systems problem in agent-directed KV management and history-dependent cache reuse.
2hv9iSTRak.main_concern: Accuracy comparisons change both context policy and cache mechanism, leaving the contribution of direct KV editing unresolved.

pH6aMrCD8T.one_liner: Loss-response eigendirections rescale retained low-rank factors through validation-gated post-compression calibration.
pH6aMrCD8T.problem: Preserving low-rank directions during compression does not ensure that their magnitudes suit the language-modeling loss.
pH6aMrCD8T.method: LENS builds a response matrix from first-order loss changes under directional rescaling and selects its eigendirections. A quadratic surrogate proposes relative gains with a shared scale; held-out loss validation gates updates folded into existing factors.
pH6aMrCD8T.key_idea: Rescale retained low-rank directions along loss-response eigenvectors, accepting changes only when held-out loss decreases.
pH6aMrCD8T.evidence: Reviews cite first-order theoretical justification, local-descent results, and experiments across several LLM backbones and low-rank compression methods.
pH6aMrCD8T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find post-compression directional calibration well motivated and report broadly consistent empirical improvements.
pH6aMrCD8T.main_concern: Reviewers request explicit runtime and memory accounting for gradient profiling, eigendecompositions, scale search, and validation.

Nj0xzBbbka.one_liner: Per-image, per-block secret frames encode equal-magnitude diffusion watermarks while preserving the Gaussian noise prior.
Nj0xzBbbka.problem: Initial-noise diffusion watermarks must preserve Gaussian noise while surviving generation and edits, but pipeline-specific noise assumptions complicate comparison.
Nj0xzBbbka.method: The analysis characterizes prior preservation through Gram invariants and recovery through random consistent frames. ESM uses equal-magnitude modulation with separate frames for each image block, regenerated from a key and per-image nonce.
Nj0xzBbbka.key_idea: Encode equal-magnitude watermark coordinates in independently regenerated secret frames for every block of every image.
Nj0xzBbbka.evidence: Theory analyzes prior preservation and sign errors, while SD1.5 and SD2.1-base experiments test JPEG50, cross-watermark recovery prediction, and cropping.
Nj0xzBbbka.claimed_gains: Under JPEG50, ESM recovers 114/128 and 110/128 complete 512-bit messages on SD1.5 and SD2.1-base, versus 69/128 and 74/128 for half-normal modulation.
Nj0xzBbbka.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified theoretical account of prior preservation, frame sharing, and decoding behavior.
Nj0xzBbbka.main_concern: The evaluation supplies the correct per-image nonce externally without establishing practical nonce retrieval or verification behavior.

teYqJCmnJA.one_liner: Pairing conversations with users' self-reported reasons and reactions supplies data for user modeling and assistant personalization.
teYqJCmnJA.problem: Conversation datasets record messages but omit users' stated motivations and reactions behind those messages.
teYqJCmnJA.method: ThoughtTrace collects multi-turn human–AI conversations alongside first-person reasons for prompts and reactions to responses. It uses these annotations for behavior prediction and thought-guided response rewrites for personalized-assistant training.
teYqJCmnJA.key_idea: Pair each interaction with users' self-reported reasons and reactions, then condition prediction or response rewriting on those annotations.
teYqJCmnJA.evidence: The dataset covers 1,058 users, 2,206 conversations, and 10,556 thought annotations across 20 language models, with behavior-prediction and alignment experiments.
teYqJCmnJA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard in-conversation thought annotations as a useful resource for user modeling and credit the collection protocol.
teYqJCmnJA.main_concern: Downstream experiments do not clearly isolate the benefit of thought annotations or establish their practical value for personalized assistants.

d4jchANt7s.one_liner: Contextual OpenQASM 3 completion tasks and executable verification evaluate classical feedback, timing, and pulse-level quantum programming.
d4jchANt7s.problem: Quantum-code datasets inadequately cover hardware-facing OpenQASM 3 features beyond gate sequences.
d4jchANt7s.method: QASM-Eval supplies training and expert-curated test tasks for completing hardware-facing constructs within programs. An extended verifier checks syntax, measurement distributions, and execution timelines.
d4jchANt7s.key_idea: Evaluate contextual OpenQASM 3 completions with syntax checks, quantum measurement distributions, and program timelines.
d4jchANt7s.evidence: The benchmark contains 1,200 test tasks and over 4,000 training tasks, with model-size, fine-tuning, few-shot, and theme-held-out evaluations.
d4jchANt7s.claimed_gains: The abstract reports that fine-tuned Llama-3-8B outperforms zero-shot GPT-5.6-Terra and fine-tuned Llama-3-70B achieves 63.42% overall pass@1.
d4jchANt7s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing OpenQASM 3 capabilities beyond gate sequences addresses a gap in quantum-code evaluation.
d4jchANt7s.main_concern: Reviewers question whether template-generated tasks and their expert validation establish reliable performance on independently written programs.

Vaa7eFKeyw.one_liner: Calibrated mixing of target and transported prediction means preserves causal targets through source-label residual correction.
Vaa7eFKeyw.problem: Under covariate shift, averaging predictions in the target population can estimate the predictor's mean rather than the target treatment effect.
Vaa7eFKeyw.method: TC-CPI mixes target-sample and source-transported estimates of the same prediction mean, with labeled residual correction preserving the estimand under correct fixed weights. A quadratic variance expression supplies an oracle mixing weight and independent calibration.
Vaa7eFKeyw.key_idea: Mix two unbiased prediction-mean estimates and add labeled residual correction so calibration changes variance without changing the causal estimand.
Vaa7eFKeyw.evidence: The paper supplies variance and efficiency analysis, sensitivity intervals, and allocation results, with reviews describing theory-aligned simulations and a Criteo study.
Vaa7eFKeyw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the target-preserving calibration analysis and its separation of variance benefits from transport-weight errors.
Vaa7eFKeyw.main_concern: Reviewers find the contribution insufficiently distinguished from prior prediction-powered, causal-transport, and missing-outcome methods.

ztGMzD9EPw.one_liner: Calibrating denoising timestep locations with a language-aware objective improves sampling from frozen continuous diffusion language models.
ztGMzD9EPw.problem: Few-step continuous diffusion language generation depends on timestep placement, which can alter latent states and decoded token distributions.
ztGMzD9EPw.method: StepTune searches timestep schedules on a small calibration set using a language-aware objective while fixing the model and sampling budget. It reuses the resulting schedule across inputs.
ztGMzD9EPw.key_idea: Optimize denoising timestep locations on calibration data using a language-aware objective, then reuse the fixed schedule without model updates.
ztGMzD9EPw.evidence: Experiments cover unconditional perplexity and conditional metrics across sampling budgets, including ELF and AURORA models on XSum summarization and WMT14 translation.
ztGMzD9EPw.claimed_gains: The abstract reports that 16-step sampling outperforms native 64-step sampling on XSum and WMT14 while reducing end-to-end latency by approximately 3.8×.
ztGMzD9EPw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the analysis of timestep placement and reported quality gains without model updates.
ztGMzD9EPw.main_concern: Reviewers find comparisons insufficient to separate the proposed objective's value from tuning weak native schedules or using other few-step approaches.

iHQ5uJj4SU.one_liner: Retrieves similarity-weighted residual trajectories from an external memory to calibrate frozen time-series forecasters at inference time.
iHQ5uJj4SU.problem: Frozen time-series forecasters selected by aggregate validation performance exhibit structured, input-dependent residual patterns across samples, variables, or temporal contexts.
iHQ5uJj4SU.method: Memory-Guided Test-Time Calibration (TTC) constructs an external residual memory linking compact variable-wise representations of historical look-back windows to their true-minus-predicted residual trajectories. At inference time, it retrieves similar historical variable patterns and applies similarity-weighted residual aggregation with a correction-ratio fallback to compensate base predictions without gradient updates.
iHQ5uJj4SU.key_idea: Retrieves and aggregates variable-wise residual trajectories from historically similar look-back windows in an external memory to compensate frozen predictions.
iHQ5uJj4SU.evidence: Evaluated across multiple datasets and five forecasting architectures (including iTransformer, Autoformer, and PatchTST on Exchange, Illness, and Solar), with ablations and efficiency measurements.
iHQ5uJj4SU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the residual retrieval mechanism is simple, practical, model-agnostic, and adds minimal inference overhead without requiring retraining.
iHQ5uJj4SU.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty relative to existing contextual residual-correction methods and note that building the memory from in-sample training windows leaves the source of gains and component isolation insufficiently explained.

uzSosQQzdU.one_liner: Regulates outgoing task disclosure and integrates complementary peer knowledge for privacy-aware multi-agent LLM collaboration.
uzSosQQzdU.problem: Multi-agent sharing strategies struggle to balance privacy protection with effective collaboration when agents hold different private knowledge.
uzSosQQzdU.method: The framework combines Relevance-aware Adaptive Disclosure (RAD), which governs outgoing task sharing through a self-calibrated disclosure boundary, and Complementary Expertise Integration (CEI), which filters returned peer knowledge via geometry-guided complementarity to suppress redundant reasoning.
uzSosQQzdU.key_idea: Separates multi-agent communication into a self-calibrated outgoing task disclosure boundary and geometry-guided incoming complementary knowledge selection.
uzSosQQzdU.evidence: Evaluated across medical and legal tasks on MedQA and LegalQA using both open-source and closed-source LLMs (including Qwen3-30B).
uzSosQQzdU.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 15.3% relative gains in task utility and 9.3% in privacy-utility trade-off over baselines.
uzSosQQzdU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear decomposition of outgoing disclosure and incoming knowledge selection for privacy-preserving multi-agent collaboration, along with empirical improvements on legal and medical benchmarks.
uzSosQQzdU.main_concern: Reviewers point out a potential privacy leak and implementation discrepancy in the CEI step, which requires joint access to target and peer memory representations without clarifying how private target memories remain protected.

AiFCWx9trF.one_liner: Anchors hypergraph neural network predictions on h-motif structural concepts and learnable feature prototypes with an additive interaction head.
AiFCWx9trF.problem: Post-hoc explainers for hypergraph neural networks attribute predictions to subhypergraphs or hyperedge subsets without verifying whether the identified higher-order structures drive the output.
AiFCWx9trF.method: Intervention-Verifiable Hierarchical Self-Explaining Hypergraph Neural Network (IV-SENN) represents higher-order topology via fixed h-motifs and recurring feature patterns via learnable feature prototypes. An additive concept-interaction head decomposes class logits into linear, compositional, and quadratic interaction terms, enabling exact decomposition of intervention-induced logit changes for counterfactual verification.
AiFCWx9trF.key_idea: Decomposes class logits into linear, compositional, and quadratic interaction terms over h-motif structural concepts and feature prototypes to verify structural interventions.
AiFCWx9trF.evidence: Evaluated across four real-world datasets with experiments on explanation fidelity, stability, planted-signal recovery, and null-intervention controls.
AiFCWx9trF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that placing h-motifs directly into the decision path preserves higher-order structural semantics and supports unified global, local, and intervention-verifiable explanations.
AiFCWx9trF.main_concern: Reviewers note non-identifiability of structural weights due to normalized motif frequencies summing to one, potential exclusion of interaction-driven motifs during local grounding, and missing ablations isolating the h-motif encoding.

ItBVWHYcI2.one_liner: Recovers typed dependency graphs from reasoning text to drive structural RL credit assignment and targeted teacher distillation.
ItBVWHYcI2.problem: Outcome-only rewards and scalar process scores treat long-form reasoning as a linear sequence and fail to identify which non-adjacent premises support a later conclusion.
ItBVWHYcI2.method: TopoPRM recovers typed support graphs from ordinary reasoning text to supervise policy training via two mechanisms: asymmetric credit estimation (ACE) assigns structural credit under final-answer correctness constraints, and topology-guided distillation (TGD) directs a fixed teacher to revise the student's reasoning on fresh rollouts. At deployment, the student policy generates standard text without graph decoding or a verifier.
ItBVWHYcI2.key_idea: Extracts typed support graphs from reasoning chains to assign correctness-constrained structural RL credit and guide localized teacher revisions.
ItBVWHYcI2.evidence: Evaluated across four mathematics benchmarks comparing against outcome-only training and distillation-matched controls without ACE.
ItBVWHYcI2.claimed_gains: Improves pass@1 by up to 13.3 percentage points over outcome-only training while reducing mean response length by 3.8%-24.0%, and gains 2.6 points in average pass@1 using 14.8% fewer tokens against the distillation-matched w/o ACE control.
ItBVWHYcI2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that recovering dependency graphs from ordinary text to serve both RL credit assignment and localized teacher revision while keeping standard text inference is a coherent and appealing design.
ItBVWHYcI2.main_concern: Reviewers find that experimental controls do not cleanly isolate the contribution of graph topology from coarse online structural scoring, correctness-sign clipping, reward reweighting, and completion length caps.

p1W3PbBvFN.one_liner: Groups FFN neurons by visual concepts to search coarse concept paths and refine them into neuron-level ViT explanations.
p1W3PbBvFN.problem: Existing neuron-path discovery methods for Vision Transformers rely on hard-to-interpret index-only neuron IDs and require expensive per-layer searches across thousands of FFN neurons.
p1W3PbBvFN.method: The framework builds a global concept bank from attention-selected patch embeddings and partitions FFN neurons into concept-aligned groups shared across layers. It then discovers an influential concept-level path in a low-dimensional group-gated attribution space and refines each selected group to a representative neuron.
p1W3PbBvFN.key_idea: Partitions FFN neurons into concept-aligned groups to search coarse concept paths before refining each group into a representative neuron.
p1W3PbBvFN.evidence: Evaluated on ImageNet across multiple ViT variants against prior neuron-path discovery baselines.
p1W3PbBvFN.claimed_gains: Achieves 5x practical speedups over prior neuron-path baselines while finding more causally faithful neuron paths under interventions.
p1W3PbBvFN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grouping neurons by concepts speeds up cross-layer path search and improves causal faithfulness under interventions.
p1W3PbBvFN.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the dense notation and heavy reliance on the appendix for core pipeline details, along with inconsistent intervention baselines and weak evidence supporting semantic interpretability.

hUYqP8Dbut.one_liner: Selects pseudo-labels using within-strategy agreement and cross-strategy support to guide in-context reinforcement learning at test time.
hUYqP8Dbut.problem: Unsupervised in-context reinforcement learning methods typically rely on majority voting over unordered responses, ignoring structured agreement across distinct reasoning strategies.
hUYqP8Dbut.method: Structured Self-feedback In-Context Reinforcement Learning (SS-ICRL) prompts an LLM with multiple reasoning strategies and computes a Reliability-Hill (RH) score that jointly models within-strategy agreement and cross-strategy support for pseudo-label selection. It then integrates structured self-feedback into strategy-specific contextual experience across iterative optimization rounds without parameter updates.
hUYqP8Dbut.key_idea: Scores candidate answers by jointly measuring within-strategy agreement and cross-strategy support to select pseudo-labels and construct strategy-specific in-context feedback.
hUYqP8Dbut.evidence: Evaluated across mathematical reasoning benchmarks including AIME, AMC, and MATH primarily using Qwen-family LLMs.
hUYqP8Dbut.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multi-strategy consistency scoring intuitive, parameter-free, and effective on challenging math benchmarks.
hUYqP8Dbut.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons against recent training-free prompt optimization and test-time RL baselines under matched budgets, lack of analysis linking strategy support structure to true correctness, and evaluation restricted to Qwen models.

AASBoc1f7o.one_liner: Aggregates distributed natural policy gradients via Poissonized local sampling and determinant-weighted averaging to reduce finite-sample inversion bias.
AASBoc1f7o.problem: Naively averaging local empirical Natural Policy Gradient directions across data-parallel workers fails to recover the pooled-batch estimator due to finite-sample bias from Fisher matrix inversion and Fisher-gradient coupling.
AASBoc1f7o.method: Poissonized Determinantal Averaging (PDA) uses Poissonized local batch sampling at each worker and aggregates local empirical NPG directions weighted by determinants, communicating only one parameter-sized vector and one scalar per worker.
AASBoc1f7o.key_idea: Combines Poissonized local sampling with determinant-weighted aggregation of worker NPG directions to match the leading-order finite-sample bias of pooled NPG.
AASBoc1f7o.evidence: Supported by theoretical finite-worker bias and asymptotic convergence analysis, and empirically evaluated across eight MuJoCo and Procgen tasks.
AASBoc1f7o.claimed_gains: Matches the full 1/(NB) leading-order bias term of pooled Poissonized NPG with an O_N(B^-2) gap in expectation, while communicating one parameter-sized direction and one scalar per worker.
AASBoc1f7o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the finite-sample bias problem in distributed NPG is well-motivated and that the theoretical bias analysis and empirical comparisons against uniform averaging are solid.
AASBoc1f7o.main_concern: Reviewers find the theoretical novelty incremental because the method directly combines existing determinantal averaging and Poisson sampling identities from Dereziński and Mahoney (2019, 2020).

UIYAjlHyqe.one_liner: Erases target concepts in text-to-video diffusion models via tri-modal gated interventions in low-dimensional hidden-state subspaces.
UIYAjlHyqe.problem: Fixed concept-erasure interventions in text-to-video diffusion models miss transient concept appearances across frames or suppress unrelated content, degrading temporal coherence.
UIYAjlHyqe.method: CleanVideo freezes the diffusion backbone and applies adaptive interventions within low-dimensional hidden-state subspaces. A trainable gating module jointly conditions on spatiotemporal visual features, denoising timesteps, and text semantics to modulate intervention location and strength, trained with target-surrogate prompt pairs and preservation objectives.
UIYAjlHyqe.key_idea: Modulates low-dimensional subspace interventions using a trainable gate conditioned on spatiotemporal visual features, denoising timesteps, and text semantics.
UIYAjlHyqe.evidence: Evaluated on CogVideoX-2B, CogVideoX-5B, and HunyuanVideo across nudity, artistic style, and object erasure tasks, including frame-level leakage and concept recovery attack tests.
UIYAjlHyqe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning subspace erasure gates on spatiotemporal visual features, timesteps, and text prompts is well-suited for video diffusion and yields strong empirical erasure across multiple backbones.
UIYAjlHyqe.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing pipeline diagrams, incomplete reporting of adversarial prompt configurations and training compute costs, and insufficient theoretical or ablation justification for the fixed orthonormal subspace basis and tri-modal gate fusion.

dF8gEbm15s.one_liner: Diagnoses silent multilingual collapse in one-shot pruned MoEs and recovers target-language access by recomposing cached calibration views.
dF8gEbm15s.problem: One-shot expert pruning of sparse MoE models causes a silent collapse in languages absent from the calibration data, losing target-language generation access while retaining underlying task knowledge.
dF8gEbm15s.method: The authors diagnose language access versus knowledge retention through paired multilingual benchmarks and controlled expert-exchange experiments across pruning masks. They introduce COER to recompose cached calibration statistics across views and restore multilingual capability without retraining.
dF8gEbm15s.key_idea: Separates language-access experts from knowledge experts via controlled mask exchanges and recomposes cached multi-view calibration statistics to recover pruned languages training-free.
dF8gEbm15s.evidence: Evaluated across six MoE architectures (including Qwen3-30B-A3B) and four pruning scoring criteria on 2,800 parallel MMLU-ProX items and KMMLU.
dF8gEbm15s.claimed_gains: A 25%-pruned Qwen3-30B-A3B keeps English perplexity within x1.6 but loses 56 points in Korean vs. 15 in English on 2,800 MMLU-ProX items while answering 74% of Korean losses correctly in English; restoring 28% of disagreed experts closes about 80% of the Korean NLL gap and 11% of the KMMLU gap.
dF8gEbm15s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the thorough empirical diagnosis separating language access from knowledge loss in pruned MoEs and the well-controlled paired English/Korean and expert-exchange experiments.
dF8gEbm15s.main_concern: Reviewers note that the recovery method is a simple weighted-mean identity over cached statistics—effectively amounting to adding diverse calibration data—and that language coverage is confounded with broader natural-language domain coverage.

r7DgYVqy1d.one_liner: Trains a neural instance modifier to perturb TSP coordinates so deterministic heuristic constructors can sample diverse tours.
r7DgYVqy1d.problem: Traditional heuristic tour constructors for the Traveling Salesman Problem are fast but deterministic, limiting exploration and trapping solutions in local optima.
r7DgYVqy1d.method: TSP-MDF introduces a neural instance modifier that shifts node coordinates to generate multiple modified TSP instances without ground-truth supervision. A traditional deterministic heuristic constructs tours on these perturbed instances, which are then mapped back and evaluated on the original instance.
r7DgYVqy1d.key_idea: Learns to perturb node coordinates into multiple modified instances so deterministic TSP heuristics can perform guided sampling and escape local optima.
r7DgYVqy1d.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic TSP-500, TSP-1000, TSP-10000 and real-world TSPLib benchmarks using Nearest Insertion and Farthest Insertion heuristics.
r7DgYVqy1d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that perturbing coordinates to turn deterministic heuristics into sampling solvers is simple, fast to train without ground-truth labels, and consistently improves insertion heuristics.
r7DgYVqy1d.main_concern: Reviewers question the conceptual novelty given prior work on coordinate perturbation for TSP heuristics and note the lack of tuned training-free random perturbation baselines.

lZQK4G4Ktp.one_liner: Restores sample diversity in distilled diffusion generators by regressing or steering student activations along teacher principal directions.
lZQK4G4Ktp.problem: Few-step distilled image and video diffusion models suffer from severe diversity collapse across random seeds because student activation variance concentrates into fewer directions at an intermediate block during the initial denoising step.
lZQK4G4Ktp.method: The authors diagnose directional activation collapse by probing student and teacher representations, then introduce ReDiverse in two variants: ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter to regress student activations onto teacher activations, while ReDiverse-TF steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions at inference time without training.
lZQK4G4Ktp.key_idea: Reinstates missing activation variance directions in an identified intermediate block at the first denoising step via lightweight adapter regression or training-free principal-direction steering.
lZQK4G4Ktp.evidence: Evaluated across four teacher-student pairs on image and video distillation benchmarks, supported by layer-wise probing and a user study.
lZQK4G4Ktp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mechanistic activation-probing diagnosis showing that distilled models preserve total variance while collapsing effective variance directions at a specific block and initial timestep.
lZQK4G4Ktp.main_concern: Reviewers note that ReDiverse-TF requires running the teacher model on multiple noises per new prompt without reporting the computational overhead, and that a closely related teacher-student hybrid baseline is omitted.

JXYRjlh1Wh.one_liner: Trains query-conditioned distributional hypernetworks to sample multiple LoRA weight updates per input prompt at test time.
JXYRjlh1Wh.problem: Standard test-time scaling spends additional compute by sampling tokens from a fixed model rather than adapting model weights from the input query alone.
JXYRjlh1Wh.method: The authors propose query-conditioned distributional hypernetworks trained end-to-end with a differentiable Monte Carlo approximation using Gaussian regression or convex combination parameterizations. At test time, the hypernetwork predicts a distribution over LoRA adapters from the input query, enabling test-time scaling by sampling multiple weight updates.
JXYRjlh1Wh.key_idea: Predicts a query-conditioned distribution over LoRA weight updates via a hypernetwork to enable test-time scaling by sampling adapted models in weight space.
JXYRjlh1Wh.evidence: Evaluated on multiple LLM benchmarks (including MedQA, GPQA, and MMLU-STEM) across backbones such as Gemma-3-1B, Llama-3.2-1B, and Qwen3-4B.
JXYRjlh1Wh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of predicting distributions over LoRA adapters from a single query and scaling test-time compute by sampling in weight space interesting and practical.
JXYRjlh1Wh.main_concern: A reviewer identifies severe evaluation issues, noting that reported multiple-choice accuracies fall well below random chance (e.g., 9.2% on MedQA), base unadapted model scores are missing, and figures report contradictory numbers for full fine-tuning.

RSbbxTffpR.one_liner: Pretrains graph encoders by predicting continuous frozen text-encoder latents from graph representations with a query-conditioned predictor.
RSbbxTffpR.problem: Graph-language pretraining via token prediction overfits surface linguistic form, while contrastive graph-text alignment can suppress task-relevant graph features that are unnecessary for matching.
RSbbxTffpR.method: GL-JEPA uses a frozen text encoder to produce continuous target embeddings for text descriptions and trains a predictor to reconstruct these latent targets from graph states. For downstream tasks, query conditioning allows the predictor to extract task-specific information from the frozen graph encoder.
RSbbxTffpR.key_idea: Reconstructs continuous frozen text-description embeddings from graph states in latent space and conditions the predictor on downstream queries.
RSbbxTffpR.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic and WikiBio feature-suppression diagnostics, node-, link-, and graph-level tasks, and query-conditioned graph question answering across nine tasks.
RSbbxTffpR.claimed_gains: Improves by 25.2-43.8 percentage points the rate at which two valid descriptions outrank a negative compared to token prediction, and achieves 95.6% probe accuracy on a target-relevant factor versus 12.7% for alignment with easy negatives.
RSbbxTffpR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that applying a joint-embedding predictive architecture to predict continuous text latents from graphs is clearly presented and outperforms easy-negative contrastive alignment across multiple graph tasks.
RSbbxTffpR.main_concern: Reviewers note that feature suppression in contrastive alignment disappears when using hard negatives (which reach 99.9%-100% probe accuracy, outperforming GL-JEPA) and view the architecture as an incremental combination of GraphJEPA and GraphCLIP.

sWeIACQ9IK.one_liner: Introduces a 300-question benchmark with verified web searchability and expert subgoals for evaluating multimodal web-browsing agents.
sWeIACQ9IK.problem: Existing benchmarks for multimodal browsing agents lack multi-hop cross-modal task complexity, verified public searchability of visual evidence, and intermediate process evaluation.
sWeIACQ9IK.method: The authors construct BrowseComp-V3, a benchmark of 300 manually curated multi-hop questions across diverse domains with archived publicly searchable evidence and expert-validated subgoals for process-level scoring. They also provide OmniSeeker, a ReAct-based multimodal browsing agent framework for standardized evaluation.
sWeIACQ9IK.key_idea: Pairs 300 multi-hop cross-modal web-browsing questions with verified publicly searchable visual evidence and expert-annotated intermediate subgoals for process evaluation.
sWeIACQ9IK.evidence: Evaluates a broad range of proprietary and open-source MLLMs and browsing systems (including OpenAI Deep Research, GPT-5.2-Thinking, and Qwen3.6-Plus with OmniSeeker) with tool and oracle ablations.
sWeIACQ9IK.claimed_gains: OpenAI Deep Research, the best-performing proprietary system evaluated, achieves a success rate of 56% on BrowseComp-V3.
sWeIACQ9IK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the verified public searchability of distributed visual evidence and the inclusion of expert-validated subgoals for intermediate process evaluation.
sWeIACQ9IK.main_concern: Reviewers highlight mathematical inconsistencies between domain-level and overall scores in Table 2, question the small dataset size (300 questions across 24 subdomains), and ask whether predefined subgoal paths penalize valid alternative search trajectories.

38ZbF4Gdhx.one_liner: Models diachronic lexical semantic change by linking period-specific contextual mixture components via balanced optimal transport and Markov composition.
38ZbF4Gdhx.problem: Scalar lexical-semantic-change scores obscure when meaning shifts occur, which usage senses contribute, and whether change stems from shifting sense prevalence or within-sense reorganization.
38ZbF4Gdhx.method: Coupled Usage-Sense Processes (CUSP) fits mixture components to contextual word embeddings in each time period and couples adjacent periods using balanced optimal transport composed into a Markov process. Displacement operators quantify overall change and timing while decomposing squared variation into component-center movement and within-component reorganization.
38ZbF4Gdhx.key_idea: Composes balanced optimal transport couplings across period-specific contextual mixture models to decompose semantic variation into component-center shift and within-component reorganization.
38ZbF4Gdhx.evidence: Supported by parametric recovery proofs under Gaussian-mixture assumptions and evaluated on synthetic data, English and German DWUG, the Janus benchmark, and court opinions using XL-LEXEME embeddings.
38ZbF4Gdhx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the optimal-transport Markov composition mathematically coherent and appreciate that it unifies magnitude, timing, and sense-level decomposition of lexical semantic change.
38ZbF4Gdhx.main_concern: Reviewers question the linguistic validity of balanced optimal transport when sense frequencies shift (forcing probability mass to transfer between distinct coexisting senses) and note that the full decomposition shows no clear empirical gain over the mean trace or existing baselines on DWUG.

z17hPeUzks.one_liner: Trains a multi-agent runtime failure auditor by perturbing its internal representation operators to generate hard latent trajectory variants.
z17hPeUzks.problem: Training runtime failure auditors for LLM multi-agent systems from fixed trajectory corpora is bottlenecked by costly rollout collection and lacks a mechanism to target execution prefixes the current auditor finds hard to classify.
z17hPeUzks.method: Dream2Discern alternates between two phases on a fixed trajectory dataset: during Dream, it applies bounded low-rank perturbations to the auditor's representation operators to maximize prediction loss on recorded execution prefixes; during Discern, the auditor trains on these hard latent variants using the original terminal outcome labels.
z17hPeUzks.key_idea: Perturbs the auditor's internal representation operators to maximize prediction loss on execution prefixes, generating renewable hard latent variants without collecting new trajectories.
z17hPeUzks.evidence: Evaluated on AFTRAJ-2K and StepShield across Qwen3 and Llama backbones against failure-auditor baselines and closed-source LLM judges.
z17hPeUzks.claimed_gains: Achieves over 90% trajectory-level weighted accuracy on both AFTRAJ-2K and StepShield.
z17hPeUzks.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that runtime failure prediction for multi-agent trajectories is an important problem and that the learned auditor achieves strong accuracy on AFTRAJ-2K and StepShield.
z17hPeUzks.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ablations show the unperturbed LoRA auditor or random perturbations already match or beat the Dream perturbation strategy in most settings, alongside concerns about train-test task-group overlap on AFTRAJ-2K and similarity to adversarial weight perturbation (AWP/SAM).

0OBmrCcqFB.one_liner: Generates pseudo-labels via non-equilibrium graph diffusion and refines unsupervised camouflaged object detectors with stochastic relative preference optimization.
0OBmrCcqFB.problem: Unsupervised camouflaged object detection suffers from visual entanglement and intra-object multi-camouflage, causing fragmented initial pseudo-labels and confirmation bias during self-training.
0OBmrCcqFB.method: The DES-UCOD framework introduces Non-Equilibrium Diffusion Pseudo-labelling (NEDP), which aggregates transient multi-spectral modes prior to global equilibrium to form structural pseudo-label anchors, and Stochastic Relative Preference Optimisation (S-RPO), a reward-driven sampling strategy that mitigates pseudo-label noise.
0OBmrCcqFB.key_idea: Captures transient non-equilibrium spectral diffusion dynamics to unify fragmented camouflage cues into pseudo-labels and optimizes the detector via reward-driven relative preference sampling.
0OBmrCcqFB.evidence: Evaluated across four camouflaged object detection benchmarks (including COD10K) using a DINOv2 backbone, with pseudo-label diagnostics across 4,026 training images.
0OBmrCcqFB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the framework achieves consistent quantitative gains across four camouflaged object detection benchmarks and improves initial pseudo-label quality.
0OBmrCcqFB.main_concern: Reviewers note that the non-equilibrium diffusion formulation lacks an unweighted (t=0) baseline to separate finite-time diffusion dynamics from simple spectral mode truncation, and that S-RPO lacks isolated ablations.

XFHXlREKbQ.one_liner: Probes frozen LLM internal states without token decoding to detect both harmful content and context-dependent unsafe tool use.
XFHXlREKbQ.problem: Existing LLM guard models are designed for message-level content moderation and perform near chance at detecting context-dependent unsafe tool calls in agent trajectories.
XFHXlREKbQ.method: The authors analyze open-source guard models and show that harmful content and unsafe tool use are linearly readable along nearly orthogonal internal directions. They introduce TACIT, a lightweight readout trained on a frozen backbone's intermediate internal states that classifies trajectory safety without decoding tokens.
XFHXlREKbQ.key_idea: Trains a token-free readout on intermediate hidden states of a frozen LLM backbone to capture orthogonal internal directions for harmful content and unsafe tool use.
XFHXlREKbQ.evidence: Evaluated across two model backbones and six agent safety benchmarks, including controlled paired tool-schema degradation tests, unused-tool placebos, and leave-one-benchmark-out transfer.
XFHXlREKbQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear distinction between harmful content and unsafe tool use, the careful paired-trajectory and placebo-tool probing analysis, and the efficiency of classifying safety from internal states without decoding.
XFHXlREKbQ.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the headline comparison is confounded because TACIT is trained on in-domain splits of the target benchmarks whereas baseline guard models are evaluated zero-shot off the shelf.

QMbOqNupOH.one_liner: Co-generates reasoning trajectories with a frozen junior model during RLVR while updating only senior tokens via GRPO.
QMbOqNupOH.problem: Language models fine-tuned alone with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) suffer from policy drift that degrades their compatibility and handoff performance when collaborating with weaker partner models.
QMbOqNupOH.method: Tandem RLVR (TRLVR) pairs a trainable senior model with a frozen junior model to co-generate reasoning trajectories under step-level handoffs. The standard GRPO objective with verifiable task rewards is applied exclusively to tokens emitted by the senior model.
QMbOqNupOH.key_idea: Applies GRPO updates only to senior-emitted tokens on trajectories co-generated with a frozen junior model to preserve cross-model handoff compatibility and legibility.
QMbOqNupOH.evidence: Evaluated by training Qwen3-4B-Instruct on competition mathematics and testing solo reasoning, reasoning-step handoff robustness, token-level junior legibility, and zero-shot handoffs with smaller unseen junior models across four math benchmarks.
QMbOqNupOH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that embedding a frozen junior into reward-bearing rollouts is a clean, regularization-free way to maintain partner compatibility and handoff accuracy in RLVR without hurting solo math reasoning.
QMbOqNupOH.main_concern: Reviewers note that the tandem-training paradigm with a frozen junior and token masking was already proposed in prior work, and that training experiments are limited to a single backbone (Qwen3-4B-Instruct) on math tasks.

jvrq9c1Y4a.one_liner: Guides LLM heuristic evolution for multi-objective combinatorial optimization using tool-based solver trajectory inspection and an adaptive observation policy.
jvrq9c1Y4a.problem: Automatic heuristic design for multi-objective combinatorial optimization typically relies on aggregate scalar performance feedback, obscuring how search progress, stagnation, and coverage loss vary across Pareto trade-off regions over time.
jvrq9c1Y4a.method: TRACE-EA uses an LLM observer to query trajectory indicators recorded during candidate evaluation inside a multi-objective evolutionary solver to diagnose weaknesses and generate heuristic variations.
